title: Exclusive Interview with Alex Wright
text: great friend of the program, pretty dang good defensive end joining us. Alex Wright in studio. We were just talking off air. You're you're the old head out there, buddy. You're one. How does that land about you look around and it's like, okay, I'm one of them. It's, you know, Denzel and Grant who were, you know, little limited for Denzel and obviously Grant didn't participate today, but was out there, but you're the you're the veteran out there, man. >> I guess life goes by fast. It >> does, doesn't it? >> Yeah, it sure does. I mean, like when they told me that the careers in football, like the years go by and by, like my rookie year felt so long compared to like being in college and then year two went by, then year three went by, then year four, and now it's like you looking back, I'm in year five already. Like that's it's like it's a blessing, don't get me wrong, but it's just like you look back and it's like, wow. Like, so I mean, I just try not to take it for granted. I don't, you know, I take it day by day, uh, period by period in practice and just try to be like a leader to like the young guys and stuff like that. It's hard saying it's hard like saying I'm a young guy or I'm a vet now because it's like >> you're 25. >> Yeah, exactly. So like >> you're 25 years old. >> But at the same time is we we we preach in the the D line room. It don't matter how old you are. It don't matter how you know how cuz that was the that was the the the stigma on me when I came in. I was a pup. I was you know I got to get stronger. Wasn't supposed to play yet. This that the third and then it's like now it's just like that has changed. If you can play you can play. And if you it no matter how old you are. So, I just try to be a vet. It's funny saying that like like I was just talking to Grant. It's funny hearing that and the years and stuff, but at the same time, it's like we still got to stand out. I'd have been here long enough. But I know the offense is going to get right and I know the defense we we still going to hit our strides. So, I mean, just because, you know, we don't have the same people anymore like 95, but at the same time, it's like we still have a standard here. So, >> what was that? I mean, obviously that's going to affect you know, your room as much as any other. What was it like kind of getting that news and then, you know, now you've gotten to be around Jared, but what was it just like kind of for you just getting the news and and seeing how that all went down? >> Man, you know, I went viral because of that with Adam. Adam posted me saying that. >> Oh, really? >> No, I didn't see that. >> Yeah, he posted He was like cuz I told him I'm I'm not going to say what I was drinking but but um I had got the news and I was in the kitchen uh just talking to I think like my family uh just a few people and stuff like that just on the phone just regular and I'm just scrolling on Twitter uh and you know thing is fake cuz you know Twitter posts fake stuff all the time all the time all the time all the time. So I'm like this is I'm like yeah yeah but something told me like somebody was talking about yeah they was talking about Miles might get traded and I'm like please Miles is a Brown for life like anyway when I when I hear that it's like bro I bro we let's be real he's a Brown for life. So I'm scrolling and then I'm scrolling. I'm like, "Okay, might as well got trade." And I get a notification. Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa. Notification. You seen the trade? Then Adam Sheff was three. I remember vivid. It was three alarm emojis and it said bombshell. Miles got traded and instantly I stood out like I went outside on the back patio. My dogs just like running around. I'm like, "Whoa, whoa, whoa, whoa. Let me call. Let me call. Let me call my mom. Let me call people." So that happened and then people was like, "You see the trade? You see this? You see that?" I'm like, "What just happened?" Like I I was shocked. I was shocked. I couldn't cuz I was hellbent cuz when people asked me and stuff like, "You think M's going get traded?" I'm like, "Bro, no. I don't think M's going to get traded." At the same time, it's like >> he's a one of one. >> Yes. >> And and and the term and the term generational athlete is used too loosely in my opinion. Like >> he truly is. >> He truly is like one of one. So in my head, you see like with Joel and and Miles, like you see Del in the indoor, you going to see the banners like they going to be next up. So like when I when I seen it, I'm just like, bro, >> like I I was shocked for for a cool few hours. And then people was text me like, yeah, like that's your room now. Like hearing that messed me up more than a mile straight because it's like, okay, I'm growing up. But at the same time, it's like it came quicker than I thought. But at the same time, it's like, "Hey, I'll be all right." But eventually, as the day went on, I felt better about it. I started looking towards the future. >> I knew it was gonna mess me up because I I was with Miles for >> four years. >> Yeah. >> So, for the vet, I'm thinking, you know, he's up there with Miles, he go to he's like 40, but you know, I'm thinking when he's retiring, I'm older and stuff like that. And then now it's like, man, like I really grew up with him. >> Yeah. And then to see him go like that though, it kind of like it kind of threw me off a little bit. I can't even lie. >> Yeah, you've se you are young, but you've seen a lot. The 22 season, which was your rookie season, was a very interesting season for a variety of reasons, but also for you coming from UAB and, you know, getting into the NFL game, then you have an excellent end to your second season. >> Now, you can also say, well, I've had the injury and I busted my butt. You come back, you have a career year coming off of that injury, get the next contract, which congratulations again. >> Appreciate it. >> And now all of a sudden, you've seen that the best player in the world can be traded. Like you've seen you've gotten business, you've gotten injury, perseverance, >> you've seen it all. >> And the only thing I can say is playoffs. >> Yeah. One thing I can say is like >> as much as much as the business can get personal, it's still business at the end of the day. So that's where once I once I like tapped in mentally was like it's still a business like it don't matter who you are like it's like you said it happens to the best of them rarely but >> it still happens. So like I said uh when when we had the practices the next day the OTAAS the next day and you know and like I told the defense I said you know it's going to feel different. It's going to feel very different like you're not going to see Miles walking around here no more like you've been seeing the last few years or whoever that just got here. You may not see Miles. You're not going to see Miles. You know, I know y'all was planning to see Miles, but it's not going to happen. Like Grant, Denzel, I know y'all was used to the handshakes with with Miles and stuff on the field and you know, just but it's not going to be like that no more. So, but at the end of the day, it's like we can't dwell on the past though. It's going to suck, but we can't dwell on on >> We can't take for granted what he's did for this organization. We can't we can't we we can't we can't not look at we can't we can't not look over that. >> Yeah. So, but I did tell them, I know, just just don't ignore it. Don't ignore the the weird vibe. Don't ignore because like I told him when I was up here on Monday before the trade happened, it was too quiet in the building. Like I'm like, "Yeah, it's quiet, but it's too quiet." >> But I said at the end of day like we were at the golf course. >> We all found out like in our carts >> in the carts. >> And uh I I was saying I was like, "Yeah, at the end of the day, we going to be all right." >> Yes. It's gonna suck because he's not here, but at the same time, we are all professional athletes, man. >> What did it mean for you? Uh that that that deal shocked us. It shocked Jared Verse, too, right? Two-time Pro Bowl guy with the Rams and probably thinks he's going to be a franchise guy with the Rams. >> This goes down on a Monday. He flies here on a Tuesday and he's at OTAAS on a Wednesday. >> What? How I mean, it's quick. That's less than a week from right now. How has he fit in jumping into this situation? >> Man, I asked him, you know, I didn't even I didn't even ask about football when he first got here, you know. I asked him like, "Okay, how are you?" Because I never experienced that. I seen people get traded. I seen people get cut. I seen people retired like, but me personally, I never went through that. But, uh, I asked him like, "How are you? Like, how how you feel right now?" Like, not as far as football, but like mentally because I know you was balling over there and stuff, but he was just like, you know, man, I was shocked. Like, I can't even lie. Like, I was I was shocked. I was upset. I was, you know, cuz, you know, I didn't have in my mind on being traded and stuff like >> Um, but I didn't try to make it >> instantly about football because I know that's that was he was getting ready to to build his life over there. >> So, um, but once we got that conversation out the way, man, and we took it to football, we took it to football, we took it to, you know, just our mentality and what we see like what the standard is and stuff like that. And he fit right in. Like he he he's out there being talkative in practice. He's out there pushing the young guys like we pushing young guys. Me and him are having our own conversations and walkthroughs and team periods and uh indie practices and stuff like that. Uh so we just trying to build the chemistry up as far as like him just getting him and getting him used to our defense. But you can see he already has flashes in our defense now. >> So just for him and the standard that he brings and the mentality that his bring that he brings like it matches what we do here. So with that I don't see no problem with him fitting in at all. like he's going to be the same person that he was in LA if not even more because now he has a chip on his shoulder because it's like okay you traded me now I'm going to show you why you shouldn't trade me. So at the end of day we all rooting for Jared. We all want him to come in and be not only the best Jared version of who he is but at the same time just keep keep being consistent and keep being who he is off the field too. Did that say something to you guys that you know and the reality is it's kind of it was such a weird thing with Miles getting traded because we just hadn't seen him because he hadn't been at the OTAAS and so it was almost like it happened >> not even in real life. You know what I mean? It's not like oh when somebody leaves the building and you oh goodbye you know >> what did it say to you guys though that Jared got a plane and was like I'm practicing on Wednesday because he could have listen >> he could have stood out just >> yes the Rams are were in a very good situation. they think they're going for a Super Bowl, all of that. He comes here and he was like all about work and that the first day just watching you guys go out there, it was awesome. >> I mean, that just shows the type of person he is. Like it's like he's it's no man left behind. Like, and it's the fact that it's like I don't want to watch out. Like, I want to come out here and and and see what I'm a part of now and what can I bring to the table and help us. So, at the end of the day, like with with him, like I said, it's his mentality, it's his mindset, it's his demeanor, it's the way he carry himself. Like one thing about Jared that he's he's very confident within himself. So at the end of the day once you and everybody knows like in this league like if you don't have confidence you don't have like you might as well not step on the field man. So >> I mean at the end of the day he is just like man like he's going to be a baller because the way that he comes out like he comes out he takes we all take everything serious. Uh he like I said he pushes everybody. He pushes me I push him. At the end of the day, like we both the same age. So, it's like we have something special here that people may not, you know, really know about or like get used to. So, it's like the fact that we building the chemistry now. And like the fact I want to build the chemistry with my teammates that I just got here, I still want to keep knowing names and getting used to being around people and stuff like that. Like, I get it messed me up, but at the same time, it's like the more I get used to this and I get used to you guys, I'll be all right. >> You've said this a couple of times uh since we've been chatting here about the standard and upholding the standard. Obviously, we haven't chatted since the changes and the coaching and all of that stuff and new defensive coordinator obviously, but a lot of familiar faces. You mentioned Jock still in your room, B. Lynch and his, Tarvin and his. So, that you've mentioned the standard a lot and while we've had some changes, that stays and and that's something you pick up on not just from you, but some of the other guys we've talked to that that the way this defense has played over the last several years, that stays the same no matter the changes. Yeah, I feel like, like I said, we can't ignore 23 sacks. We can't. That's just that's just >> Nobody's ever done it. >> If we going to do that, then we might It's like the blind leading the blind. We just acting acting ignorant and all this other stuff. But at the same time, it's like we had how many sex overall this whole year >> as a team? >> As a team >> last year. Hold. Please keep going. I'll give >> top three. >> Yeah. I think it was north of 50 if my recollection is correct. So my thing is it's like yeah you can't ignore 23 sacks but at the same time everybody had a job to do out there on the field. Wasn't just me. It wasn't just Malik. It wasn't just Mason. It wasn't just Miles. It wasn't just the the back seven. Wasn't just anybody. At the end of the day we took it upon ourselves to to make plays. You know if we if the offense couldn't make a play, then we got to make a play. If we couldn't make a play, then the offense make a play. But at the same time, that's what we're trying to do as a whole now is just get everybody all in. No matter what what play what position you play. >> You can be a wide receiver and we going to push you out there in the team. I'm going to push you out there in team cuz that's just the the leadership mentality that I develop coming from Miles and and Denzel and you know just like the old heads like even with Malik. Malik Malik may not talk a lot but at the same time >> we'll be over there in Indie and Malika you know he'll be on he'll be on us. Just because I'm year five, that don't mean he's still not gonna teach me. I can still be a sponge. You can never not learn to love. >> Yeah. Yeah. >> So, um it's just like it's it's it's just getting up, waking up, looking yourself in the mirror, and telling yourself what type of day it's going to be. And that's what I try to tell tell the young guys. It's like, you have an opportunity, man. >> Like, not a lot of people get this opportunity in life. It's a lot of people that want your job. There's a lot of people that's on that's out there on the street that's that's willing and willing to do whatever to just get an opportunity to come in and just produce. So, at the end of the day, you have to treat this job like it's the most important thing in the world. Now, family is family, like outside the building. But once you step in this building, you have to have your thinking cap on. You have to go. You have to be confident. You have to do everything you can to like you have to do everything you can and have what it takes just to withho with withhold of what we're doing here. Like we we have something that's going here. Like I said, it doesn't matter how old you are. It doesn't matter how young you are. If you can play ball, you can play ball, but we also going to push you, too. So, we don't settle for anything. So, >> 53 was the number of sacks last year by the Cleveland Browns defense. 53. Want to flip it around for you're on the other side. This is a new look offense. I I've said a lot and my opinion is I think this defense is going to be excellent again this football season. This offense has a chance to take step forward investment in the draft all that. Todd Monkin was brought here to get this offense going through your eyes on the defense. You're seeing it more. What are you seeing from this offense and are you encouraged by some of the the playmakers and what you're seeing? >> I'm seeing accountability. I'm seeing players push players. I'm feeling like a new energy of like a sense of urgency. >> Like I'm seeing a lot like and it's a new system so it's like you know everybody has this this kinks and whatnot of getting used to it. >> Sure. >> But >> the way we talk trash to them and you now since I've been here they never talk trash back from my opinion. But you feel you feel the vibe is different. Like the vibe is different. Quan I'm talking junk to I'm talking jump to Shadore. Like I'm talking jump to the tight ends to the tackles just just and then just hearing them just fire back. It's like we got fight like we like I haven't seen we had fight in a long time man. So and I genuinely feel that way like I I'm not going to come up here and just sit here and just just say something just for just for the hell of it. No. Like >> when we talking trash and you know we just feeling like the sense of urgency and stuff like that and they holding each other accountable. The O line is holding each other accountable. Uh Deuce is firing everybody up. Todd is firing everybody up. It's just like even when even when Todd is getting into the trash talking too, that's how you know like, okay, we we growing like we growing a whole lot closer than what I thought we could be. So, I mean, we just building a bond, not only as a brotherhood cuz it's a lot of new faces around here. Yeah. >> Like like we we we >> went deep into the O line. We we got new signings. We got young players coming in, young hungry player uh hungry players coming in, offense and defense. So, it's like at the end of everybody has just one goal in common. Let's just get better every day. So, >> Alex, I think um you mentioned that sometimes it feels weird to refer yourself as a vet at 25. You sound like a vet. You act you act like a vet. You lead like a vet. We're lucky to have you. Thanks for stopping by, buddy. It's great seeing you as always.

title: Recapping 2026 OTAs and Mandatory Minicamp | Buffalo Bills

title: Why David 'Knuckles' Montgomery is the key chesspiece for Texans offense: 'He can do it all'
text: Hey guys, Aaron Wilson. We're talking about the new identity of the Texans offense. A smashmouth identity built around bellcow running back David Montgomery. Almost like a throwback, a boxer. I mean, this guy downhill punishing runner, and they brought him in for a very specific purpose to create a legitimate running game. Last year with Woody Marks, out of necessity, they made him the number one running back. And he's RB1 only because Nick Chubb was absolutely washed. So, that became clear when there was no explosiveness, not as much tackle breaking as the past for a five-time Pro Bowl running back that really was signed as an emergency when Joe Mixon and his mysterious foot injury just completely unraveled the running game. Not having Mixon, a Pro Bowl runner the year previous to this one, you had a absence of a physical presence. Stroud with five interceptions and five fumbles in two playoff games. And you saw it the week before. It was there. It was there against Pittsburgh Steelers. title: Aaron Glenn Mandatory Minicamp Press Conference (6/18) | New York Jets
text: All right, good morning. Um hope everybody's doing well. Uh so obviously I canceled practice today. Um had the players come in. We had our We had our team meeting. Uh which we discussed things that went on throughout the the off season. And some expectations of what I want from the guys as they come back. Um but listen, the guys have given me, the coaching staff, even themselves and their teammates everything that I asked of them um throughout these phases. The uh participation has been outstanding. Um the work they've put in has been outstanding. Um and I like exactly where we're at. And when I say that, I told those guys is I want to get to the point where I love where we're at. And we know that um when you get to when you want to love it, it's going to take some time. So we know exactly uh the things that we have to do to improve in that in those areas. Um but I do like where we're at and looking forward to to the for some downtime and then getting to training camp and get to the point to where I love exactly where we are as a team. So um Any questions? >> Hey Angie, what what was your message to the team in terms of >> I pointed those things out to those guys because I want them to get away from it. Um but once they do get back to it, let's make sure we focus on these terms and phrases that we talked about throughout the off season. Then once we get back in the training camp, I really want to define exactly what the messaging would be in training camp. But I didn't go too much into that cuz I want those guys to really focus on those those terms and phrases that we talked about. And then once we get into training camp, man, we'll really break down those things that we talked about that point. So we talked in depth about those things and then let the players out. >> Just AG spinning it forward to training camp. Could you describe I mean, is it going to be different from last year? How how it might be different from last year's camp and the the tone you're trying to set this year? Is it going to be different structurally? I know last year you did a lot of a lot of hitting emphasizing tackling. Is it going to be pretty much, you know, a repeat of that or you got some new wrinkles in store? >> Um you have some new wrinkles. I'm a big fan of of not having the same thing over. I want to be able to shock the player's system of doing things different. And sometimes those things can happen, you know, at the spur of the moment, you know, because I see exactly how the team is operating that day. So I don't want to sit here and just say, "Okay, we're going to be this, this, and that." The only thing I want to do is say, "Listen, we're going to work our ass off." There's some things that I want to make sure that I emphasize as far as competitive stamina, I think we've talked about before. There's some things about being intentional on how we practice in the situation that we want to practice. I will continue to do that, but I don't want practice to get to a point to where it's redundant to where it's just, "Okay, the players getting this zone to where, okay, man, we're going to do this." No, I'm always shock the system somehow. Those some things that we're doing as we get to training camp. >> AG, how much progress do you feel like you've made, the organization has made, you know, since January? The >> Yeah. >> the roster, the whole thing, everything that you and Louis when you guys sat down after Buffalo, after the exit interviews, and you said this is what we need to do this offseason. How much progress do you feel like you've made? >> I think we made a ton of progress. Um and I would go back from um right after the season and me evaluating myself, uh the things that I want to get better at, the things that I want to do, the the direction I want this team and organization to go in. Um and then right after that, we got into free agency. And all that we talked about this. I love [clears throat] the players that we brought in. Um everything was intentional as far as what type of players that we want to bring in. And then going to the draft, and all the work that was put in the draft. And again, um Mooge and his staff have given me the information that I need to be able to look at all the players that we want to get. And then for us to come out of the draft with a with the players that we actually fell in love with. Um and then going from that to rookie mini camp to off season program. Um and again, I like exactly where we at again, but between myself and the players, this is just not me. Myself and the players, we want to get to the point that we love exactly where we at. And we know that takes time. Um and we'll see that happen as we get into training camp. >> Have you seen enough from the backup quarterbacks this spring to make you feel confident that one of them could be your number two this year? >> Well, I would say this. Um we're always going to create competition when it comes to that. And the thing is um we had Bailey who's been around this league for a long time. He's won some games. Uh we have Cook that was with us last year who's still a rookie, who's still developing, who's a second year player, and he's still developing. And then we had Kay who was doing a really good job, you know, until he uh he was out with the back. And uh he was going to get a chance to practice today um to see exactly where he was going to be at. So, uh I would say this, those guys are going to continue to compete. I would never sit here at this time of the the and say, "Okay, this guy's going to be our backup quarterback." Guys, we have training camp to go through, you know, so um but I think I've said that before. Those guys going to compete and see who actually uh comes out of put uh with that fight. >> AG, do you like that balance on the roster of youth and then adding these veterans in the offseason? Did you see the influences already of DeMario, Geno, Minka, guys like that paying off inside the locker room? Like what kind of uh impressions are they having on this group? >> Yeah. Um and again, that was one of the things that we were very intentional about as far as bringing in guys that's that's been around uh that's played at a high level and not just played at high level, but has led at a high level. Um so yes, I I I I'm extremely happy with the amount of youth that we have. I think we were the second youngest team in the league last year and then bringing in a number of veterans that's been there, done that. But not [clears throat] just that, but also been really good players in this league and understand what it takes to win and how to win. So um it was very intentional trying to create that. Um but not just just that in itself, but bringing in good players that's going to help elevate this this franchise to where it needs to be. >> AG, we we focus on the players, obviously, but this stretch, you know, particularly the last two days and then leading up to it, for you as a coach, getting out there on the field with, you know, guys like Frank Reich and and Dookie and and kind of building that on-field coaching rapport, how important has this stretch been for you kind of getting to know these guys on the field, too? >> Yeah. Yeah, well, I I've known both of those guys for for a long time. Obviously, Duke was with me in Detroit for a a number of years. Um so that relationship was already there. Uh Frank, as far as just knowing exactly who he is as as a man, um the personal part of it, I knew really, really well, but then again, after I got a chance to understand him as a coach, man, that just just I got more excited, you know, when you see how detailed he is. Um, just his mentality on allowing the players to be themselves uh as far as the instinctual part of it, but also make sure they're disciplined as far as what uh what they do. So, um it's been important to make sure that we do that, but we just don't do it on the field. We also do that in meeting rooms to make sure that we're on the same page. >> Take a couple more. >> AJ, what do you see from David Bailey this spring? What makes you say he's dropping in and >> What's going to be the most important thing for him in his first training camp? >> Yeah, so I think David has grown quite a bit. Obviously, the thing that that I think we all know that stands out is his first step quickness and his ability rush the passer. Obviously, we don't have pads on, so the physical part of it we just couldn't see, but we do know this. Um, the way he strikes the bag, his length, how strong he is. Again, he's 250 some pounds. I have no worries about, you know, anything else about his his weaknesses cuz I know he's going to work his ass off to be able to to to get better at those things. Um, so listen, I'm looking forward to this player. Man, he's going to be a damn good player for us. I think Dunbar and Cam has done a really good job of of coaching him out there and he's very receptive to the coaching too. So, he's going to be a good player for us. >> Uh, what do you What are you doing in the next 6 weeks? >> Aaron, what do you get away at all or what do you do for fun during the spring? >> Um, it's funny cuz I was just talking about that with a couple other gentlemen. Uh, it's I um, I have this tendency and I get I and I got this from my dad. My dad passed uh a years ago. Um, but my dad was a workaholic. That's that's what he did. Um, she going to have 10 brothers and sisters and my mom never worked. So, all I seen my dad do was work. So, I actually took on that trait of being a workaholic. Um but my wife does a really good job of of trying to get me balanced and making sure I have things outside of football to um to create a hobby. So, I'll golf. and then I'll go to the country, man, and just just hang out and um mess with horses and um do things like that. So, that's my that's my happy place. >> Thanks, coach. Thanks for everything. >> Appreciate it.

I know next week Adam we're going to have our annual NFC East draft podcast series where we draft a team from both offense and defense just from NFC East players and then we're also going to do a look at some of the players who are going to enter training camp under the rate, you know, kind of the guys who are under pressure and we're going to say why it's really important they perform in training camp and things like that. I mean, not too many not too close but weeks four weeks away but the time we get to Greg Cosell it'll be even sooner than that. So >> Love it. Awesome. >> Good. Yeah. >> That's what I really love it. Looking forward to it. >> Me too. That's going to do it for this episode of Inside the Birds, the leading podcast and Eagles Intel. title: Football at Four: DiCecco's Eagles Notebook and Listener Email Bag
text: And football at four is powered by the Inside the Birds podcast and it is brought to you by the Fanatic Sportsbook at Ocean Casino Resort in Atlantic City. The go-to game day destination. Huge screens, great drinks, and all the sportsbook action you want. It's the perfect place to catch every play and celebrate every win. I'm sure with the Phillies and Mets going at it this weekend including tonight. No game tomorrow because of the World Cup, but you can watch all the World Cup action and the Phillies and Mets action this weekend at the Fanatic Sportsbook and of course, it is the place with big screens, big bets. Game day hits different at Ocean. To learn more, visit the oceanac.com. All right, Andrew Di Cecco is here from the Inside the Birds podcast. We are into the summer which means we have our Inside the Birds football at four summer mailbag questions we've been compiling all off season long. You can always send them in on the White Horse RV text board 403-0973. When you have Eagles questions, you can text or email or send them to me at Mike Gill Show. We've been compiling our summer Eagles mailbag questions for the guys and today in the hot seat, it's Andrew Di Cecco from the Inside the Birds podcast as he has our football at four summer mailbag questions. What's going on, Andrew? >> Hey, Mike. How are you? I'm doing great. >> We're doing good, man. And a lot of questions building up in the mailbag as we count down to training camp. I think Adam said on Friday's show we are about five weeks away to Eagles training camp. So here we go. We got a lot of questions for you, Andrew. Here we go. Let's get the first one. This one's from Dave in Somers Point. He first off, Andrew, love your appearances. He asked this question. With A.J. Brown gone, DeVonta Smith is here. Who do you look at? He says, "My question is how do all these pieces fit together? Who takes that number uh two and three spot at wide receiver uh during training camp?" >> Yeah, well, first off, Dave, I appreciate the kind words. And and then, when you look at this wide receiver group, they have a lot of diversity in terms of what they can bring from a skill set perspective. Obviously, Devonte Smith will be the top option there. But then, depending on how you look at it, I view Rakim Jarrett as an inside slot receiver. He can play outside, but predominantly, I imagine he's going to operate outside of the slot. Do I think he'll command more targets than the third player I'm going to mention in Dontayvion Wicks? Yeah, probably. But I I think Dontayvion Wicks gives you that bigger body receiver that you're going to want on the field more often than not. He can be that boundary X type of player, 6'1" 206 lb. He's more of a short-to-intermediate guy who can separate at the top of routes and be sort of a safety valve of sorts. I think Rakim Jarrett, to that end, could also fill that role as well as as being someone who can work the middle of the field, but he can also catch and run and create yards after the catch. So, I think if you're looking at it in terms of target share, Rakim Jarrett would be the number two, but Dontayvion Wicks gives you a little bit more flexibility in terms of what you can do um from a personnel perspective. And uh so, I I think that's kind of the way you're going to see it shape up. >> All right, uh this one is from uh Sam over in Egg Harbor Township. Uh he says, "Yo, Andrew, help me figure this out. We brought in Woolen and Jonathan Jones. We have Mitchell. Cooper DeJean looks like he's going to safety. Do you think the corners are going to be better this season?" >> Yo, Sam. Yes, I do believe so. And so, Riq Woolen, and take this with a grain of salt, of course, because it is spring practices, was the standout player there. You don't often see corners who are 6'4" who can move the way that he can. His ball skills were apparent. You saw or I saw what his skill set could provide in confined spaces in the red zone. But, we'll see what happens when the pads come on. Now, I think the secondary is going to be better because when you add a player like that who can solidify that second spot that has been a position of turbulence for the goals, it stabilizes it. You have a a solid pairing opposite Quinyon Mitchell, and it allows Vic Fangio to be a little bit more flexible in terms of what he can do with personnel. And he mentioned Jonathan Jones, and I really appreciate that because that's a player that probably is flying a little bit under the radar, but I view that as perhaps the Eagles' most underrated of the one-year signings, meaning that he can step in and play inside, he can play outside. If you need him to step in and play safety in a pinch, he can do that. He's played at a high level throughout his career. Now, he's a little bit older, so his play has tapered off, but he's played in playoff games, and now you have sort of a buffer where you don't have to rely on Keele Ringo or Jacorian Bennett to step in should an injury surface. Now, you have a veteran who's going to give you a a competent level of production when he's on the field. There's demonstrated performance there. So, with Jonathan Jones, I think that gives you another piece that that takes the secondary to another level. Is there an area of opportunity there at the safety position? Perhaps, but you can't pay everybody. They're not going to have all pros across the board. The Eagles are bullish on Drew sample and his second-year potential. Marcus Epps is a player that Vic Fangio spoke glowingly about. He's someone that you can depend on. You you know that he's going to be assignment sound and find himself at the right place at the right time. He gives you a little something to be desired when it comes to the athletic piece, but I like Michael Carter quite a bit. I I've always liked him when he was with the Jets. He moves well. He's really sharp-minded in terms of his football intellect, and he can cover some ground. And so the modern NFL safety needs to be able to do that and be able to be sort of a movable chess piece. He can do that. We need to see how he transitions full-time to safety when the pads come on, how does he handle the the wear and tear demands of that position. He's a smaller guy at 5'10", 185 lbs, but I like the components that the Eagles have sort of added to complement what they have in Quez Watkins and Cooper DeJean, and I think they're all going to fit together pretty well in terms of the overall picture. >> All right, Andrew DiCecco answering your summer mailbag questions. This one is from Chris in Dennis Township. Says, "Andrew, I noticed Dallas Goedert grant Calcaterra, uh and they drafted Eli Stowers out of Vanderbilt. Do you look at that as a luxury pick uh or is this more indication of a lot of 12 personnel?" >> Well, I do believe it's going to be an indication of a lot more 12 personnel. That's sort of the the influences in the background that Sean Mannion's coming in with and to maybe a lesser degree, might even see some 13 personnel. But I believe that where the Eagles took Eli Stowers, that was right around where he was widely projected to go. I don't think that that was necessarily viewed as a luxury pick as much as it is setting yourself up for the future and adding another player that you can move around. He offers alignment versatility and he's a little bit of a work in progress as a blocker. That should be expected. That wasn't really his calling card at the collegiate level. He was their top receiving option, so he didn't need to do that as much. But I I like the collection of tight ends that they brought in. Dallas Goedert, I think, stands to benefit greatly when you look at how the Packers used Tucker Kraft and Luke Musgrave. And then you have Johnny Mundt who can be that blocker. Eli Stowers, while I don't expect him to sizable role as a rookie because he is limited in terms of his blocking, I think that there are going to be moments where you can see it come to fruition. You can see the Eagles vision come to come to fruition in terms of how they move him around in the mismatches they can create with them. But then, next season of course, they pass the baton in all likelihood to Eli Stowers to be the tight end of the future. >> All right, Andrew. Let's see what Steven Mayes Landing says. He says, "Andrew, let's go around the division. Dallas, Washington, Daniel's is back and the Giants are the Giants. Do you look at the Eagles as an overwhelming favorite in the NFC East this year or do one of these teams worry you?" >> Well, I like what some of the division rivals in terms of the New York Giants adding a John Harbaugh, adding I believe Matt Nagy's over there now. So, you have some structure in place, coaches that are going to give you a baseline. And the the Cowboys, I thought that was a home run hire for Christian Parker at defensive coordinator. That was their problem. The offense hasn't been an issue for Dallas. It's been the defensive side of the field or side of the ball where they've been really leaky in coverage. They've squandered opportunities to close out games as a result. And when you bring in someone like Christian Parker who articulates his vision exceptionally, he's a young coach. So, I think ability component that that should be taken into account. I I think that they've done a nice job of adding some young pieces that kind of fit the mold of what he's looking for. I like what Dallas has done. So, to answer that question as succinctly as possible, I think that Dallas will be a team to certainly keep an eye on while I believe that the Commanders with now with a healthy Jayden sorry Jayden Daniels and and then you have the the Giants. They're still a couple years away I think from being a a viable contender in any capacity. But the Dallas Cowboys because they've they've shored up that defensive side at least right now on paper, I think that that's a team to certainly earmark as as one to follow along. >> the Washington thing. We were talking about this yesterday a little bit Andrew where it feels almost like when they had Robert Griffin the third that first year it felt like oh my God you're going to have to deal with this guy for 10 years and then after that it was like you hope Jayden Daniels for a football fan bounces back and really thrives but you hope he doesn't go down that RG3 cuz he is a smaller guy. >> Yeah, he has a slight frame the way that he plays it lends itself to taking some big hits and I would also say that Jackson Dart if he doesn't alter the way that he plays he's going to be more susceptible to injuries. Also not the biggest guy in the world is a little reckless reckless in how you know, he doesn't necessarily have the same awareness or presence of mind of Jalen Hurts where I didn't think he took a lot of hits when he was on the move. Jackson Dart for longevity purposes and Jayden Daniels need to find a way otherwise it's going to be something I would imagine similar to what you outlined with Robert Griffin the third. You hope to never see that because you saw the potential but I think the way that both of those young quarterbacks play that's that's where the long-term projection becomes a little murky because you don't quite have that certainty with their health. >> All right, this one's from Sal out in Hamilton. As Sal in Hamilton that sounds like a perfect match there. Hey DeCicco, what is your vibe on the offensive line this season? We all know health was a problem there. So what do you got? I know you saw a little bit of them in OTA. You don't really get to see them do much there but what's your vibe on the offensive line? >> Yeah Sal, I love this question and you don't really get to fully gauge what they're doing on the field because they're not running the football that much in spring practices are pretty much geared towards the the passing game but what I did glean is the optimism and eagerness with from whether it was Lane Johnson, Cam Jurgens, Jordan Mailata about sort of embracing this new system and how it's going to accentuate what they do from an athletic standpoint, but also from a health perspective. Lane Johnson just seemed and and Cam Jurgens, they just seemed refreshed, reinvigorated, and I believe that that's going to to really translate onto the field in uh you know, the dog days of summer when the pads come on and they're really ironing out some things and and and pinpointing what they want to do in terms of the the run schematics and things like that. So, I think there should be a lot of uh enthusiasm and optimism as it surrounds the offensive line. They didn't drop off in terms of talent. As we all know, they're uh they fell you know, the the pitfall there was attrition. And for the Eagles offense to really take flight, it doesn't necessarily matter all that much if Sean Mannion's uh the evil genius that Jordan Mailata built him as or if Saquon Barkley um looks to be a little bit more spry if they don't have the offensive line of 2024 or even something comparable to that, it's not going to matter what this offense looks like. The key to their success is up front there in the trenches, and I think right now there's a lot of reason and and just reading, you know, body language and things like that. >> Uh all right, let's go to uh this one is from Rick over in Egg Harbor City. Um has to do with the edge rushing. Jordan Davis a huge addition, but Nolan Smith, Jaelan Phillips Hunt, which guy uh do you think will have a bigger impact this year? >> Oh, uh Jaelan Phillips Hunt to me. Jaelan Phillips Hunt and Moro Ojomo, I've sort of pinpointed as my two defensive breakout candidates that become household names at the end of this season. So, Jaelan Phillips Hunt to to really uh offer a different perspective here. He played 693 snaps last season. That was 452 more snaps than he played as a rookie and he led the Eagles edge rushers in snaps, sacks, quarterback hits, and he led the defense in interceptions. He also tied with Jordan Davis in tackles for loss, which I believe was nine. So, this is a player who's who took a a pretty uh sizable leap from year one to year two and Vic Fangio spoke pretty highly of Jalen Hurts and his progression saying, "He just needs to keep doing what he's doing. Uh he's going to keep getting better and better. That's what you want to hear. That's what you see when you when you're watching him out there on the field in the spring. And while you're not seeing the the hand-to-hand combat where he's, you know, battling offensive tackles or anything like that, there's no pads in the spring, but you can see uh the size that he's put on, the refinement in terms of his his pass rush plan, and he talked about his attention to detail being the biggest difference in his game and pretty learning how to react learn to react and and just his sets and things like that. So, Jalen Hurts Hunt now also goes into this season playing opposite Josh Sweat and Bernard. And he was sort of unlocked a little bit in week 10 when the Eagles added Josh Sweat and Bernard at the trade deadline where he had five and a half sacks down the stretch just one prior to the arrival of of Jay uh Jaylen Phillips. So, I think now you're going to see Jaylen Hurts Hunt really turn the corner in year three and and push for double-digit sacks. >> All right. Uh couple more on our summer mailbag questions for the guys from Inside the Birds. Andrew Di Cecco's in the hot seat today and Chris in Ocean City says, "With all the recent stuff around the Birds, is it a Super Bowl or bust type of season for Nick Sirianni?" >> Uh that that that's such a hard question to answer because I I I don't know that that that would be the case. You want to see strides made offensively. You want to see the defense continue its ascent, and I do believe that they're going to be among the NFL's elite, certainly with the pieces that they've added. And then you also have the the storyline of it being the third season with Vic Fangio, and many of the core players on that group are entering their third season playing together. That being said, I I I to say Super Bowl or bust for Nick Sirianni, I think that's I think that's a little strong. Now, the roster as it's currently constituted, as long as they stay healthy, there's there's not much of a reason why, barring the offense just not meeting expectations, uh making a a deeper run in the postseason. And I think that they're going to do that, and that should be the ultimate measure of success. As long as you don't see a lot of the prevailing themes that we've seen over the past couple years and the shortcomings of the passing game sort of reveal itself, I I I think that that should be viewed as a success- successful season, Super Bowl or not. >> All right, let's get one more in from Seth in Washington Township here, and uh he says, "Why do you think that uh Jalen Carter has not gotten an extension yet?" >> Well, you have the shoulder thing that you want to maybe see how he returns from that. There This is a sizable investment that they're talking about here, and no one's going to dispute that Jalen Carter, when healthy, has been a centerpiece on this Eagles defense. But then you also have the maturity component. Can't get tossed out of a game, spitting on the quarterback. You have to make sure that you're you're following in line with the team's core values and and not letting your emotions get the best of you. So, this to me, I mean, and they did, you know, pick I I I If I'm the Eagles, I want to see how Jalen Carter bounces back, and what are you seeing from him in terms of overall growth? I've been pretty clear of my bullishness for Jalen Carter. I think he has the ability, and had it not been for last season, you know, he's he should be viewed among the top defensive tackles in football. And when you look at what he can do from collapsing the pocket, commanding double teams, it opens so many other things up for his teammates to feast. But, I think that kind of speaks to why they're waiting. They want to see how he looks in his return from the shoulders and and you want to see him continue to grow in terms of maturity as well. So, that it's kind of a of a multi-faceted, multi-layered discussion, but that would be my my immediate thoughts there. >> All right, we got the summer mailbag questions for the guys. Keep them coming in at Mike Gill Show. Text board on the White Horse RV text board 609-403-0973. Email, of course, as always, Andrew's back on Thursday. Adam's here tomorrow. Jeff will be back on Monday for a Mosher Monday mailbag. Great questions as we lead into training camp. We'll also have our division previews coming up. We'll take a look at all the teams in the NFL and that will lead us right in to week one right here on Football at Four. Andrew, we'll summer mailbag for you. Looking forward to next week, man. >> Appreciate the questions, everybody. Thanks, Mike. >> Andrew Di Cecco, everybody. Make sure you check out the Inside the Birds podcast on all podcasting platforms and don't forget to check out all the games at the Fanatics Sportsbook at Ocean Casino Resort in Atlantic City. Big screens, big bets, game day hits different. You want to see Matt Rife July 24th and 25th at Ocean Casino Resort. Joey Diaz is there on August 7th and Sebastian Maniscalco September 17th through the 20th and 24th through the 27th. That's all over at Ocean Casino Resort in Atlantic City. I am Mike Gill. This is the Sports Bash. Keep our summer mailbag football at four theme going. We'll do that again on Monday with a Mosher Monday mailbag here. And of course, you can get your questions answered from the guys from the Inside the Birds podcast each and every week on Football at Four.

title: Minicamp Roundup: ‘Off to a Good Start’ | Bucs Insider | Tampa Bay Buccaneers
text: We've got a few more signings to dive into. >> This confus continues to evolve as the season goes on. >> Welcome into Buccaneers Insider presented by Hard Rock Bet Sports Book. Casey Phillips here with senior writer and editor Scott Smith and we have a mini camp in the books. It means we are finally at that weird dead bedtime break. Kind of the only time all year that there's just >> dead time here. Coaches, players go on their vacations and it's this this was the last bit of football before training camp. It was funny to go into the cafeteria, the dining room after practice yesterday and like no players were in there cuz they didn't have meetings after practice. So they were out of here for like 6 weeks. See you later. >> See you later. Yep. And so uh it's great to get a chance for us to recap a little bit of mini camp and it was a little more mini than we originally anticipated. Uh similar to last week where one day got cancelceled although for different reasons. Uh, so what did uh what did coach Bull say about the two-day mini camp and then the reason for it only being two? >> Well, I mean I would say general observations about the camp, not just Coach Bulls, but everybody, Baker included, we'll hear from him, but um I know this is an intangible and it's hard to prove, but there's a there was a noticeable le higher level of energy and intensity and not just in mini camp, but in the OTAAS and that's why they lost a practice because they were getting a little intense and too many players ended up on the ground at one particular practice. And so the NFL said, "No, that's too much contact. We're taking away." That's really, we talked about that before. It's really not that uncommon. Um, and it wasn't the desired outcome, but it also was sort of not the worst thing in the world because it showed how intense these guys are and how hard they're working. And I think it it was a concerted effort by the team. We talked about it all throughout the spring to and and um Jason Light said it many times to bring in uh players that had a certain edge, intensity, and nastiness. and and Baker used the word that begins with a that I probably not shouldn't say on this show. U you know, so uh that's showing up and it's only going to get way more intense in training camp because then you can put on pads and you're not trying to tackle guys, but you are allowed to hit. Yeah. >> And so I think it's just a sign of things to come. But as you mentioned, it was a slightly shorter mini camp and I'll just go ahead and let coach Bulls explain why. >> Uh we had a good practice. Tomorrow's practice was going to be more of the younger guys anyway and they got a lot of reps today, especially closing it out in two minutes. So, we feel good where we are. I think they did a good did a good job working working together. They put in the work in phase one, two, and three as well as mini camp here. So, we're off to a good start that way. Obviously, a lot more work to do. Very pleased with how we ended where we are and for the most part keeping the soft tissue injuries down. I thought they did a good job coming and training that hard. So getting the scheme down and everything else was part of it and preparing for it and I thought they did a good job there. course. >> So, it was on Wednesday morning that we got the word officially that um coach had canceled Thursday's practice and and the whole day, not just practice meetings. And um it's >> it's not really again, it's not that unprecedented. You see around leagues, some teams canled their entire mini camps and I think a little bit of a tidbit of what coach said right at the end there is telling um we for we were fortunate enough to uh mostly escape any soft tissue injuries, hamstring poles, things like that. And uh I think that kind of goes into the the motivation for teams um when they do cancel one or or several practices. It's just like we've gotten this far and nobody's hurt and we really want to get to training camp with their roster healthy. >> Let's not take our chances one more day. And we've seen it. We've seen guys get hurt in the last drill of the last practice before regular season. Happened to collage one year. So I can understand that motivation. And he did talk a little, we're not going to listen to it, but he did talk a little bit later about the changes the team has done to try to avoid those injuries because we had a lot of them last year, right? And it involves um you know when they lift, when they lift heavy, when they lift light, when they do a lot of leg work, how much they're running and and you said it's not all cutting back. Some of it is actually adding on to certain things. But, you know, there on one side you have the fact that you can't necessarily avoid injuries completely. somebody's just going to have a freak accident, have an injury. But on the other hand, there is the science going into trying to limit >> the chances, the possibility of it happening. So that's the Bucks are very much trying to do that. Let's cross our fingers and hope it works. >> Yep. And so you talked about the mini camp schedule. Well, now we also have the training camp schedule because again, that's the next thing on the horizon. The team did announce, of course, there's a bunch of different types of practices in terms of who they're open to, themes that are going on. So, we wanted to make sure you had all seen this so you could kind of start planning and plotting certain days that you might want to show up. And of course, we always love to see as many of you as possible out there. Training camp is just such a unique opportunity to be so up close to the players that I don't care where your seat is in the stadium. You are not going to necessarily be as close as like feet away from these guys as you are here. And and it's just a really cool opportunity. you're watching guys fight for either starting roles, backup roles, and we have a lot of things that go on outside of the practices themselves. There's things for kids to do. It's a great familyfriendly activity. So, make sure you you mark down those uh schedules as well. >> My understanding is that um we've had feedback from the players about training camp practices and they prefer it with the fans there. >> Yeah, I I'm sure it's like it's a rough stretch and to have that boost of energy has got to really help. >> I was a little bit surprised. I thought maybe there was a sort of that insul insular feeling like come on this is team we're just we don't need to be but no they actually prefer and eight may seem like not a huge number of open practices but the reason for that is there's fewer practices in Tampa because of the expected plans well I think the Jets are already set and I think they're working on the Jaguars and expect that to happen to have joint training camp practices in the weeks on the road against those two teams before preseason games. So those are multiple days taken away from practice being here. >> Yeah. >> So still the majority of the practices here are open to one group or another. And check it out on like you said on buckaneers.com and other places um just to get it to the date straight. And also um all the practices except for one night practice which we do every year are start at 8:30 in the morning and parking is free and you do have to there's dates on there that tell you when and how to do it but you do have to get a digital ticket um which uh the proceeds all go to charity and it's not a lot. >> That's great. Um all right so now let's let's go a little bit to some of our reactions from mini camp. We got to hear from you played a soundbite from coach BS earlier but there were also several players we got to hear from. Uh, I know Baker, you know, few people had gotten to talk to him at the end of his camp last week, but he spoke again uh to the media this week. What were some of the things that you feel like you you got to hear from him? >> I think my favorite one was when he was asked about the team being concerned about him putting his health on the line, you know, like the scrambling too much or taking too many hits or whatever, which by the way, a lot of times when these storylines develop that the team is concerned, it's because Jason Lighter tubs were asked a question. >> Yeah. do you think that Baker, you know, does he need to avoid taking more hits? And then they just generally the answer is something like, well, you know, that's part of who he is and we don't want him to get hurt. We want him to make good decisions, but it's not like Jason Light is going out there spreading the word like, you know, trying >> Baker's got to do this differently. >> And so Baker says he was kind of tur about it and I I get it. He's like, I played 17 games every single game for the past three seasons. I don't think this should be a question. >> Yeah. And look, I love I love when Baker gets a little irritated. I do too. >> I think everybody on the team loves it. So, you know, whatever works at this point. If now it's about him proving that he can still play this way and make it through, great. >> But another good part was I talked about it earlier about the intensity level of practice and if you don't want to believe me that it's true, you can believe Baker and here he is talking about that and it's coming a lot from the defensive side. Yeah, there's definitely a lot more energy, I think. And it's [cough and clears throat] when you lose guys that have been here for a long time, um like Levante and Mike and Dean and just others, uh forget a few names, but people kind of wait around and wait for those guys to make a play or say something. And when you get new faces and obviously Nacho's been here before, but you get guys that come in and spark a new energy, uh maybe it's trash talk or just the way they approach the game, it's it uplifts everybody. And so it's been really fun to see. Um obviously all the new pieces on defense that that in itself brings a lot of energy and so it's made every single practice competitive. Um obviously we had a had a day taken away just but that's that's the type of energy and uh you know competition that we're having right now which is really good for for the Bucks. Yeah, I I love hearing about the energy and it it kind of tied into what I wanted to talk about where Antoine Winfield Jr. took the podium and uh he talked about a lot of different things, but a couple things that I really liked was just him talking about some of the new additions up front >> and you know, we've talked to like Yaya and heard his excitement about things like Ruben Bane getting brought in or Aan Robinson of how much that'll help him maybe not get doubleteamed as much, whatever. But all those additions up front also really help your secondary and everybody else if they're getting in there. And then also again the attitude they bring is helpful as well. So Antoine had a few different things to say about that. Let's listen. >> It'll help a lot. Um you know the game starts up front. So if you have a dominant front seven it makes everybody's job way easier and if they can control the game then we'll we'll be better off this this season. >> It's fun. It's uh it's great to hear. You know you love to see it out of the guys and you want to play with guys that are chirping a little bit. you know, it builds that, you know, intensity and um, you know, we just kind of follow suit with that. So, it's nice to have that on the team. >> You know, um, he's talking about how obviously a a good defensive front helps out the secondary, but what really helps out is when that front is only rushing four and still getting to the quarterback. That can make such a huge difference for a defense if it if a front four can do that um, on a consistent basis. and David Walker that also talked. Now, just to recap, David Walker fourth round draft pick, looked awesome in practices in uh OTAAS in training camp and then torn ACL and was done didn't get to play his rookie season and has had to rehab ever since. title: UFL 'has a purpose' as NFL's developmental league | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: The NFL doesn't have a developmental league, but it kind of does. There is a place for the UFL. And as I've said recently, the UFL is thriving at its own level. Now, how high can it go? We don't know. Nearly a million viewers for the United Bowl up against a World Cup match on Saturday, that's pretty good. In this day and age to get nearly a million people together at the same time watching a network, that's pretty good. Their ratings were up a little bit this year compared to last year. Their attendance was down, but look, the money's in the TV. It's not in the the box office. It's not like these are World Cup ticket prices to go see a UFL game, but they're doing enough. And they're developing talent. Sean Payton, the Broncos coach, talked about that yesterday. They're always looking to see who's developing talent. Is it the CFL? Is it the UFL? Is it some other FL? But because the NFL doesn't have a developmental league and hasn't had one for nearly 20 years, there's there's a purpose for the UFL. A bigger purpose. You know, the World League used to develop guys. Kurt Warner was there. Brad Johnson was there. It gave coaches opportunities. It gave officials opportunities. It gave executives opportunities. And from time to time you hear the argument that the NFL should have a developmental league. Well, the NFL would if they thought they would make money from it. They don't think they'll make money from it. That's why they pulled the plug on NFL Europe. They weren't making enough profit from it. If a minor league was viewed as profitable to the National Football League, they would start one and they would be playing. They could play in season. You know what they could do? I just thought of this. If they did this the right way, if they created a wholly integrated subsidiary under the NFL that would be the NFL minor league. And it was wholly owned and operated by the league itself. How you could play Friday and Saturday games without worrying about antitrust. Now, it could get complicated and it could be kind of a clever and risky move, but my point is this. There are plenty of opportunities during the season to have other football. There are clear opportunities out of football season to have football. You could have a minor league system in season. You could have a minor league system out of season. They would do it if they thought they could make money from it. And the question is how much money is the UFL really making? They keep the costs low. I don't know what the revenue is, but they made it through 3 years. Before that, the UFL had a couple seasons. The XFL had some stops and starts. COVID was a factor, but spring football has been a regular thing since 2019. Remember the AAF? They ran out of money and they died halfway through the season, but I think this whole appetite for spring football flows from the very very basic reality that with gambling legalized, people need things to bet on. And I haven't seen any of the numbers about wagering on UFL, but it's something else to bet on in an age where gambling is legal. And people are watching. Not NFL numbers, but you know, their full season rating was higher than the average rating for NHL games. So, they're doing okay. And at some point, you have to ask yourself, does the NFL get more actively involved? And at some point, does the NFL explore creating its own league or even buying the UFL and turning it into something bigger? The NFL is always looking to grow the pie. Grow the pie. You know, they want football season to be as long as it can be. Maximum inventory. Let's keep adding weeks. What if you had a viable spring league that that caught fire. You put the NFL logo on it and off you go. If they thought they could make money from it, they would do it. My question is based upon what we're seeing from the UFL, are they going to take a closer look? Now, I know they're going to try to do something with flag football, but I'm talking about true minor league developmental pro tackle football. It would be good for the NFL teams, for players to get these reps and coaches and executives and referees, but if you make money, they would definitely do it. Hi, it's Mike Florio. Thanks for watching PFT on YouTube. Hit subscribe for the latest news and analysis from Pro Football Talk.

title: Texas Tech gave Brendan Sorsby 'more than a nudge' to leave for NFL | Pro Football Talk | NFL on NBC
text: I want to start today with something that has become very clear. In the paperwork that was filed by Sorsby's lawyers dismissing the lawsuit that resulted in the injunction that on the surface allowed him to play in 2026, they said unequivocally on Monday, June 15, Texas Tech told Sorsby he would not play in 2026. Once you hear that, you got no choice. The Big 12 caved. After they got sued, not the Big 12, Texas Tech caved. After the Big 12 sued Texas Tech, Texas Tech knew they had no way out. They knew that there was nothing good that was going to come from it, and they used the teammates card on Brandon Sorsby. There's a clip floating around from billionaire Cody Campbell who apparently runs the show at Texas Tech, and he's trying to run the show in college football. But the idea that, you know, this hurts your teammates, too. It's very easy to push the buttons of a player. But the reality is it does hurt his teammates. They all would have this cloud hanging over them all season long. When is the rug going to get pulled out from under us? And even before the season starts, what's the latest development in Sorsby versus the NCAA, Big 12 versus Texas Tech, this person versus that person? What does it all mean? Could they get to a point where they just pull Sorey B off the field? Could they get to a point where they don't make it to the Big 12? For far too long in college football, the players didn't make business decisions. So, that's the good news. He was able to make a decision for himself what's right to do. title: Where will Sorsby be drafted? + UFL becoming new developmental league | PFTPM (FULL) | NFL on NBC
text: It's Thursday, it's June 18, and it's PFTPM. Almost through week one of the PFT live hiatus, and we're at the point where the offseason programs are over. In theory, nothing should be going on until training camp opens. Yeah, there's still some draft picks that need to be signed. And we know there'll be different things that happen. Guys will have appearances. They'll say something there. They'll do something here. There's always a chance someone's going to get in trouble. So, we are constantly on watch even as the news flow trickles to basically nothing. But this year, oh, there's something thanks to Brendan Sorsby, thanks to the supplemental draft, the first time since 2019 that a player will be picked in the supplemental draft. That is going to consume a lot of the conversation as we get into the month of July. So, it's something I'm going to keep talking about, mainly because there aren't many other things, but there are so many threads that still need to be pulled. And I want to start today with something that has become very clear. Now, Monday night when the news broke that Brendan Sorsby was entering the supplemental draft, I had heard this, but I didn't say it as directly as I could because I wasn't 100% sure that it was accurate. But his agent, Ron Slavven, was on 1053, The Fan in Dallas on Wednesday, and he said, now he tried to soften it by saying it was a 50-50 decision between Sorsby and Texas Tech for him to enter the supplemental draft. Texas Tech gave him a nudge. They gave more than a nudge. in the paperwork that was filed by Sorsby's lawyers dismissing the lawsuit that resulted in the injunction that on the surface allowed him to play in 2026. They said unequivocally on Monday, June 15, Texas Tech told Sorsby he would not play in 2026. Once you hear that, you got no choice. The Big 12 caved after they got sued. Not the Big 12. Texas Tech caved. After the Big 12 sued Texas Tech, Texas Tech knew they had no way out. They knew that there was nothing good that was going to come from it. And they used the teammates card on Brendan Sorsby. There's a clip floating around from billionaire Cody Campbell who apparently runs the show at Texas Tech and he's trying to run the show in college football. But the idea that, you know, this hurts your teammates, too. It's very easy to push the buttons of a player. But the reality is it does hurt his teammates. They all would have this cloud hanging over them all season long. When is the rug going to get pulled out from under us? And even before the season starts, what's the latest development in Sorsby versus the NCAA, Big 12 versus Texas Tech, this person versus that person? What does it all mean? Could they get to a point where they just pull Sorsby off the field? Could they get to a point where they don't make it to the Big 12? Could they get to the point where they're not allowed in the CFP? There's too much uncertainty. And I think we all should have understood that this is where it was going to likely end up, especially after the outcry when Sorsby won the injunction, temporary injunction that would have allowed him to play in 2026 when all hell broke loose after that. It's just a matter of time before somebody figures out a way to put the right pressure on Texas Tech to get them to throw in the towel, which they did. And I'm not saying right or wrong. They threw in the towel. They made a business decision. Sorsby made a business decision. For far too long in college football, the players didn't make business decisions. So that's the good news. He was able to make a decision for himself. What's right to do? The bad news is he was he was put in a box. Now, in hindsight, should Jeffrey Kesler have sued not just the NCAA, but the Big 12? Do you cover all your bases? So, your injunction prevents anyone from trying to mess with Brendan Sorsby. They still would have dealt with the possibility of an appeal, and there's still a chance the appeal doesn't get resolved until after June 22. That was the ultimate risk Brendan Sorsby was taking. Set aside the Big 12 lawsuit. If He doesn't enter the supplemental draft and the NCA wins on appeal after the window closes so for 2026. No football, no team, no anything. So, he's going to the supplemental draft and there's been no indication the NFL is going to keep him out of it. The question is, will they suspend him after he's drafted the way they suspended Terrell Prior back in 2011? We don't know. And I know that there's confidence that the NFL can't do anything, but at the end of the day, the NFL is going to do whatever it wants to do. If I have learned nothing else in 25 years of doing this, the one thing I know with certainty is the NFL is always going to do what it wants to do regardless of precedent, regardless of custom and pattern and practice, they're going to do whatever they want to do. If they want to suspend Sorsby, more accurately, if the commissioner wants to suspend Sorsby, he will. So before we even get to the point of a suspension, we go forward with the draft. And I've been getting this question a lot. Where will he be drafted? Well, nobody knows. When will he be drafted? That's an even more fascinating question. Here's why. The NFL, lo and behold, does have a draft lottery. Not for the main draft. The NFL will never have a lottery for the main draft because the NFL wants to do nothing to call any attention to the connection between final standings and draft order. The first rule of Tank Club is don't talk about Tank Club. And even though they could make a lot of money from a draft lottery, it would be a massive event, 10 million viewers or more for the draft lottery. They're not going to do it because once we start down that path, then you end up in a mess. Then you legitimize this question of, oh, oh well, if we lose in week 17, we get an extra ball in the hopper for the draft lottery. They want to keep them separate for the supplemental draft. They use it. There's three categories of teams. There's the bottom chunk, six wins or less. The middle chunk, basically anybody who didn't make the playoffs, and then the playoff teams. They're going to do a weighted lottery within those three categories and then they'll stack them together. So if you're in the worst chunk, you've got a floor that still puts you ahead of category 2 and category 3. And if you're the worst team in category two, or if you end up with the lowest spot in the priority, you're still ahead of all the playoff teams. And here's why that's important. When it's time to do the supplemental draft after the order is set through this supplemental draft lottery, it's not like the normal draft with the commissioner saying the Arizona Cardinals are on the clock and then we wait however long it would be, 30 seconds, 10 seconds. Surely not 5 minutes. We wait and see if the Cardinals take anyone. And for now, the only one is Brendan Sorsby. And then it goes to the team with the second pick and then the third pick and then the fourth pick. That's not how it works. In a supplemental draft, you basically bid your pick. It's like a blind auction. You bid your pick before the round begins. And this is where it can help Sorsby get drafted higher than maybe he would have because if I'm a team that ends up at the very bottom, if I'm one of the 14 playoff teams that gets the last spot, I'm 32 and I've done my homework on Brendan Sorsby. And I love me some Brendan Sorsby. And I think Brendan Sorsby can be a franchise quarterback. and it's hard to find franchise quarterbacks and we don't have one and we need one. How do we get him? Well, if the consensus becomes he's a third round pick and that's already kind of been out there, but who knows because nobody from the teams will be telling anyone the truth in the run-up to the supplemental draft. But let's say that the thinking is round three is when someone is going to put in a bid. If I'm low, you know what that means? That means I'm putting in a bid in round two if I want this guy for the price of next year's second round pick. I get a guy who may become my franchise quarterback and it could run all the way to round one. If you have a team at the bottom of the priority that becomes determined that Sorsby can be the answer, that believes it has a great system in place to avoid any of the gambling issues, that is confident he's got it in his rearview mirror, and think of it this way. At a time when we're constantly wondering where the next gambling scandal is going to come from, isn't Brendan Sorsby the least likely guy to be in a gambling controversy? It's the guys you're not watching that can engage in mischief. Everybody's going to be watching Brendan Sorsby. He's got the apps locked out of his phone. Everybody knows. They're going to be constantly checking on him. I'd submit to you that he's less of a risk, far less of a risk than the average random player right now. That's a factor, too. So, if you're at the bottom of the priority, if you love him, and if you understand he's put this behind him, and this was just the product of the indiscretions of an 18-year-old who fell victim to years of prevalent, incessant, ubiquitous advertising aimed at getting you to grab your phone and bet $2 here, $3 here, $5 here, the crown is yours, yada yada yada. Okay, we understand how this happened. He's a product of the era. He's not a bad person. He just fell victim to advertising. Guess what? Advertising is effective. It's why they pay so much for ads. You see an ad for something on TV and you want it.
