title: Do you realize what this means for the 49ers?
text: Bottom line is that the 49ers have not had a top five defense since 2022 since Demeco Ryans left to be the head coach of the Texans. >> Or since Brandon Aiyuk and Fred Warner threw fists on the 49ers practice field. >> A two-rounder between Fred Warner and Brandon Aiyuk. >> Or since I had a beard. That was actually the first ever instant reaction. Everyone copied us after that, but Fred Warner, Brandon Aiyuk fought on the practice field training camp 2022. I did the minute-long instant reaction coming off the field and look where we're at now here in 2026. Talking about the 49ers defense falling off that you could look at the EPA expected points added ranks of the NFC West contenders last season. The glaring glaring inefficiency here, at least amongst all offenses and defenses, the 49ers defense at number 24. Seattle ended up winning 17 games, including the Super Bowl, obviously, with the number one defense and the number one special teams. That was a big differentiator between them and the Rams who had a better offense than Seattle, number two versus number 14, but a worse defense and away worse special teams. And if you watched, especially the regular season game, that is your home field advantage between LA and Seattle, it was special teams. That was the big differentiator. So, the Rams have gone out and they've tried to improve their defense. They added Trent McDuffie, Jaylen Watson, and of course, Myles Garrett. We expect them to be up in that top five defensively given those additions this year. I'm not so sure the Rams are going to hold on to number two offensively though. That side of the football, it might be more tenuous there with age for the Rams. The 49ers, meanwhile, they need to make their big move statistically on defense. And that's why you've seen the aggressive roster turnover over the past 2 years outside of the Bosa, Warner, Lenore core. The defensive line is completely different than it was back in 2024 outside of Nick Bosa. They've even seen movement at linebacker, obviously trading D Winters away. And the secondary, well, Renardo Green, the draftee in the league in that 2024 season. He's a big piece for the 49ers moving forward at outside cornerback as his 2025 Upton Stout. In totality, the 49ers have the third youngest defense now and the oldest offense. Now, there's logic behind this. The offensive renovation already underway, we'll talk about that in a little bit with obviously the 49ers have needed more speed and I think a bigger part of the renovation is going to be happening in coming offseasons. But first and foremost, they needed to address the defense because the glaring rank where the 49ers just cannot expect to sustainably compete, the one they've got to fix is on the defensive side of the ball. I think offensively they believe that they can crack into that top five with the additional speed that we'll talk about here in a couple minutes, but it's defensively where the 49ers have needed the biggest overhaul. And new defensive coordinator Raheem Morris, obviously the two biggest additions are the returns to health of Nick Bosa and Fred Warner. Osa Odighizuwa, he didn't have a good pass rushing defensive tackle last year. You were anemic in that regard last year. He comes in for the 49ers as well and they've got to try to bolster linebacker around Fred Warner and of course support the secondary as much as possible. Well, all of those ingredients, especially the fact that Raheem Morris is I think planning to modernize this defense and add wrinkles that the defense probably needs to stay ahead in chess mas- in chess matches against opposing offensive coordinators. Will all of those ingredients be able to propel the 49ers into the top 12 defensively? I think that's actually the money question of this 2026 season. Then you look at offense and elevating to the top five because I think that sitting at number six is not enough. I think the 49ers need to move from a good offense, one that managed last year, into an actually elite unit. And as you can see, um number six last year was tremendously impressive given the fact that the 49ers had so much missing from the wide receiver position to quarterback, obviously. Brock Purdy only played about half the season. So, they didn't have an explosive run game. That I think was rooted in the fact that their receivers, A, were not good separators, nor were they good blockers. So, I mean, Brandon Aiyuk really hurt this football team by not being available for the 49ers in 2025 after they invested all that money on him in 2024. But, the lack of speed, the lack of separation, the lack of blocking led to a lack of explosiveness in the run game. That led to a lack of explosiveness in the pass game because the run and the pass are tied together. So, the 49ers have pursued the solution this offseason very, very aggressively. Last year, they had to rely on Christian McCaffrey playing high-volume Superman to solve things. They had to rely on the best quarterback room in the league, Brock Purdy and Mac Jones, to solve things. And of course, Kyle Shanahan and his play-calling bound everything together. But, a year after they spent five, their first five draft picks on the defense, which was something they hadn't done since 1981, their first Super Bowl winning season, the 49ers went out and they spent big in free agency on receivers. You see Mike Evans, Christian Kirk, those are two notable names that the 49ers added that will add separation, add blocking, and in the case of Christian Kirk, add a real speed. His times last year, miles per hour times with the tracker in his shoulder pad were faster than anybody on the 49ers offense. So, that's saying something for San Francisco. And then they went out and got a 4-3 receiver in De'Shawn Stripling in the NFL draft. So, they've completely overhauled the receiver core trying to add that speed, trying to add that explosiveness. And of course, Keelan Black, the new running back, he looks explosive out Indiana and don't underestimate the power of fresh legs that Black is going to bring to the table. You combine all those things for San Francisco and I truly believe that they have the ability to be a top-five offense despite the fact that they are the oldest offense in the league. And that's the thing about the 49ers formula that some members of the national media that are talking about the age of this 49ers roster just really aren't comprehending within context. You know, older rather than younger is not necessarily better. Younger rather than older is not necessarily better. It's the right mix of both that is very important and vital for a football team to be good. You need your veteran pillars, you need your veteran leadership, and then you need your youthful energy on a team. So, a team that is just too old across the board, that's bad. A team that is too young across the board probably is not going to have the leadership and the wherewithal necessary to win a title. Finding the right mix of both is the pathway to success in the NFL and I think there are delineations between both sides of the football. In general, on defense, because you're not handling the football, it's a little less of a skill side of the the ball. That's where you can get away with the youth infusion first. And that's why the 49ers have rebuilt this the way that they're rebuilding this. First came the big defensive youth talent infusion. That is why they're the third youngest on that side. You still need your veteran pillars and that's where Bosa comes in. That is where Fred Warner comes in. It's where Deommodore Lenoir comes in. But you do need more speed. You need more energy and you know, maybe that's where Romello Height comes in for the 49ers. They also wanted ready-made rookies and Height I think is a great example of that being 25 years old, played for six different college teams. On the offensive side of the ball, everyone knows that Trent Williams won't last forever. Everyone knows Christian McCaffrey won't last forever. I mean, that's just obvious stuff. Mike Evans is going to be 33 years old this year. George Kittle is only about 10 months younger than Mike Evans. So of course, the 49ers have an older offense. It is on average the oldest in the league. But I don't think anybody is questioning the football playing abilities of Trent Williams, George Kittle, Christian McCaffrey or at least anybody with any credibility is questioning those capabilities. Those guys at some point are going to hang them up and they won't be with the 49ers forever. But as we saw last year, there's still a lot of good football in Christian McCaffrey's tank. Mike Evans, well, the 49ers are betting that he still has a lot left. He's supposedly been kicking ass for the 49ers over the course of the off-season program. Nobody could cover him. The young guys cannot keep up with Mike Evans. And you know, I would say that George Kittle probably still has something left in the tank. I wouldn't bet against a future Hall of Famer. Mostly though, I wouldn't bet against the fact that the 49ers have the one most important premium piece. And that is their quarterback, Brock Purdy. We've seen this time and time again in the NFL. Teams rise and fall, talent comes and it goes. But the teams that are able to withstand the natural roster waves of the NFL are the ones that have the quarterback, the elite quarterback, in place. And that's what the 49ers have. They've got Purdy, a young elite quarterback in place. The proof there is absolutely in the pudding. He's been at the top of NFL statistics ever since he joined the league in 2022. In fact, 2022, that's the last time the 49ers had that top-five defense. The last time I had a beard before this year. And of course, the year that we saw Brandon Aiyuk and Fred Warner fight in training camp. The birth of the instant reaction. So, everything comes full circle here about a half decade later. 49ers trying to claw back into the top five defensively because it is balance that can win a title. Balance is the keyword. Balance with a capital B. The 49ers did not have it last year. Now, one thing that bailed them out, and we cannot ignore the fact that the 49ers won 13 games in 2025, including a win over the defending world champions, the Philadelphia Eagles, on the road in the playoffs. Special teams for the 49ers. In years prior, they had been at the bottom of the league. Last year, they were behind only Seattle. Now, fittingly, ironically, I'm not sure which one applies here, but the 49ers season ended in Seattle, and it was over basically before that game began, before a snap was taken from scrimmage, because the Seahawks returned a kick for a touchdown against the 49ers. You saw the difference between the number one special teams unit in football and the number two special teams unit in football. So, special teams was a differentiator for the Seahawks over the Rams, and it was definitely a differentiator for the Seahawks over the 49ers. 49ers must keep their foot on the gas on special teams, keep it up near the top of the league. They have the most slack to pick up on the defensive side of the ball, and of course, they still want to push that offense into the tier of the elite. The reason the Seahawks and the Rams were the top two teams in the NFC last year is because they both had at least one elite phase of the game out of offense and defense. The 49ers didn't. The 49ers were good on offense and they were bad on defense. Obviously, all colored by injuries. Think if the 49ers were healthy, they could have been maybe even elite on both offense and defense. That's why Trent Williams thinks this team can be dominant if they don't have to show their resilience. But, however they get there, the 49ers need to make sure that at least one of offense or defense is elite in that top five, preferably, I would say top three here in 2026. They're closest on offense, and that's where the clock is ticking for some of these older players. But, they've got a bunch of future Hall of Famers, and they've got Brock Purdy, and who knows? Who knows where he's going to end up at the end of his career. But, he's been the best QB efficiency-wise in football since he joined in 2022. The irony is that everybody said that he had a team carrying him. He's actually been carrying the team. They haven't separated. They didn't have a run game, and they very clearly didn't have a good defense in 2025. Purdy, just like any other quarterback in the NFL, is going to need some help from the 49ers. And that's going to involve speed, separation, and a run game to get this offense into the top three. It's going to involve help from a completely modernized defense outside of Nick Bosa, Fred Warner, and Deommodore Lenoir to get that into the top 12, maybe even the top 14 would work. Look at the Seahawks. 14-1-1. The 49ers can maintain a very good special teams. Perhaps, the number three offense, the number 12 defense, and the number two special teams unit would work. Remember that this was the best division in NFL history last year. A 17-win Super Bowl champion, a 14 win NFC runner-up, and a 13 win third-place team in the 49ers who actually beat the defending world champions in the playoffs. Impressive impressive stuff in that NFC West. The Rams have obviously loaded up, but so have the 49ers. I mean, adding Omenihu, adding Mike Evans, adding Drake Greenlaw, we'll see what their draft class does. That That's not nothing. That's a lot for the 49ers. It is going to be another intense race at the top of the NFC West. And the winner will be determined by balance. Who can balance out the columns that I showed you? The last time the 49ers truly balanced out those columns, it was 2022. In 2023, their defense was number 10, and their special teams wasn't good, and it ended up costing them in the Super Bowl. 2022 was the year the 49ers had the type of balance that could win a cutthroat division like this 2026 NFC West. That's when they were number one defense. That's when they were top five offense. Special teams weren't bad that year, either. They were right middle of the pack. That's what the 49ers have to recreate. That's what this offseason has been designed around, and well, the 49ers can rest easy knowing that Brock Purdy is their quarterback to build around. But, we'll see how successful their mission of building balance has been.

Um I want to see him coming back in crazy shape, like undeniably fit to throw a great camp. Um, but part of that is getting also our timing down, you know, of the different people with different routes. It may take what one route might be for you might be a little differently what works. So, getting that connection is is important, too. >> Dan, just the entirety of the off-season back January, February when you're getting the coach staff together through this week, how do you how do you feel about it? Did you accomplish everything you wanted to? >> Yeah, I thought we really set out like with like big sights on what we could accomplish together. And it wasn't always easy, but to see the first part between, like you said, the end of the season and let's call it April 20th, how much could the staff grow? How much could they collaborate, putting in new systems, teaching it together, giving new insights, working across? We did um, examples of, you know, a coaching summit where we had other people talk to us. We've had, you know, different backgrounds, different teaching, you know, testing people under pressure, and to see that manifests itself through the teaching and the competitiveness at practice, like that made me feel good. I thought they really applied it together. I feel their connection as a group, and uh, that's really important to me to see that type of collaboration. So, I knew if they did a really good job, then the players it would get in through to them. And so, we pushed them pretty hard to get into that space. There's plenty of work to do, but I'm very excited for them, you know, coming into a training camp. What's that going to look like together? And uh, I think they all did a hell of a start with that. >> What uh, message, if any, do you leave with the guys before the the long break? >> I told them today, and we had, you know, a fun meeting this morning where we did some competitions. We saw some things from practice yesterday. It was nice to have the NFL officials here. So, we even had one that um, we had such a great clip down the sideline, so we brought the referee up in front of the team. Catch or no catch, you know, for a touchdown under review. And so, those types of things were fine. I told the team I loved the gains that they've made this offseason. And so, I spoke a little bit about what I would call like the drift, like the next 35 days, and we all could be vulnerable to that. You know, you're not here with your guys, you know, doing everything together, setting the schedule for it. But, they've got some real principles, you know, to lean back on, their teammates, the way we want to compete, you know, the standards that we have. So, I said, "By adhering to those principles here, like that that protects you from the drift." But, uh even our families are here at practice today, and so like they're all in on it, too, you know, to make sure like everybody's coming back in crazy shape to go do that and protect from the drift, which could easily happen to any of us in 35 days. But, how do we narrow it back in to make sure they need the break, the space, but also like the training to get themselves ready to really apply what they could do. it's going to be a hell of a camp. I'm certain of that. Uh just the want to, the attitude of what it is. So, it's been very good, but I got to give it a shoutout to like Chad and his staff. Like, they really pushed the pace with the players during this phase, which then pushes it again, you know, into the summer and into the training camp. >> Good afternoon, coach. >> Good afternoon. Um do you feel like, first of all, sharing the results of that uh catch or no catch uh review? >> The um rule one today was on the field. It was a no catch uh program that we came to the agreement. There was lots of discussions back and forth they but So, it was like kind of the fun part of the NFL. Like, like we could all been in the same room and had, you know, a different example. Did the ball move and not enough? And so, um by no means was it just uh one person's opinion. But, um those are fun moments to have discussions to help grow our game and the rules that we do with them. >> And I have a couple of position battles kind of want to ask you about, I know we're early in the process, but center and kicker. I just kind of how do you feel those two competitions are going right now? >> Yeah, those are like two good ones. The center one, um they're doing well. It's it's assignment and alignment to get the the techniques right, but the real battle for them will begin, you know, going against pads in the big space to go. This phase of year, I thought the three of them really did a good job, Dave, of uh new system calls, techniques, communication with the center, the protection. So, by doing that, that's going to allow them to like absolutely go for it, you know, when the camp comes to like not hold back to get And then on the kicking side, um it'll be a little bit of the same. In this part, there's, you know, just in practice kicks, we do maybe six or seven, you know, every couple days. There's been days somebody hit them all good, other days, you know, four or five out of six to go. So, I'm excited to see what that develops like, but like any other position, like let's let it battle for a while and see where it goes. It's kickoff, it's field goals. Um so, it's exciting to see what it can develop into, but uh like most things, I'll let's let's let it marinate some more and and push it through, get into preseason, where we're at with that, but it's definitely one you're on the right track of those two positions, like it's going to take a minute. >> And on that, you kind of already touched on it, but do you have like a best-case scenario if I had it my way, I'd have this battle solved by this portion of >> Probably too early for me to call. I haven't gone that far yet. more often than not, I'd like to leave leave some time to get through a preseason game into that space. So, when you get to preseason game two into that space, you're about 4 weeks out from the opener if you count that game, the next third preseason. I don't know what we exactly call like the bye before the regular season. So, that's a good space. I think anybody in any spot where they're could be coming back from injury or competitions and then having that 4-week stretch to get into that space, that would be ideal, but I also know it may not be that day and if it's a little bit after, that's okay. But, um generally, that's like a guideline that I think is worthwhile, like a four-week stretch into the start of the regular season. Yep. >> Hey Dan, um I saw an interview you gave I think with CBS the other day about last year to some degree. You said you guys weren't as connected. Uh you weren't as tough as clutch as you needed to be. What was it just about the injuries? What point did you kind of come up with that realization and how did you specifically this off season work to avoid had that happening again? when you have a tough year you want to do a lot of reflection and starting with yourself first to make sure like what parts weren't to a standard that we liked. And uh like most things there's many reasons that you want to go into that. But you also want to say, "Okay, if that's what we identified, what do you want to go work on to make sure you're putting the team back into the right space to do that?" And I've been proud of the group of the players and the coaches, their connection of what's taking place. But I did feel that and uh you know, like you don't like that when that happens, but I also wanted to acknowledge it and so the players were aware of that, too. I showed them, you know, some of those examples and uh that's been a big push for me, you know, going into this off season. So I've been very intentional about that. >> And you know, because you guys you talked a lot about culture since the moment you got here, being intentional about trying to fix things that went wrong last year, this is the time of year where teams add veteran players uh to shore up weaknesses or just to get uh move to the next step. What's that line between you need somebody to match this culture versus there's talent? >> Yeah, I think you want to lean on the that's your first filter, you know, from uh an alignment of what you want as a teammate and how that looks and kind of gave the um template of two guys that I thought have been like excellent teammates here with Rashad and uh Chesson of like their entrance into this team. And so I thought they kind of gave a good blueprint for it. So I'd say that's the standard first. And uh Adam and his staff have done a good job of making sure like that the players that we sign and bring in, you know, have been through that filter first and I can tell you as a coach like I really appreciate that that that's a part of it cuz it makes this job of connecting everybody, you know, which is already a hard one, much better when you can do that. So, that filter is up at the top first. >> Got time for three more? >> Hey coach. Could you talk a little bit about Brandon Coleman and talking to coach Singleton last week, he said that this is a guy that can probably play all five positions. How have you seen him early on? >> Yeah, and Darnell's right due to the athleticism of BC. There's plays like a screen earlier and I showed him and Kinlaw just flying out of the stack like he can run like a defensive lineman. So, I think that's referring to the athleticism. Could he be a center and climb to the next level? He's already demonstrated guard and tackle ability. We put him inside at guard in the spring and we'll do that again at the start of camp and really make sure he can like hone in on those. And so, that's what we wanted to make sure like as opposed to spreading him out cuz you can do these things, let's give him the chance to say, all right, what does left guard look like with you and Chris, much like we're doing at center. And so, after that plays itself out, you know, then we can adjust. But, it's the right call for him to make right now and like get him all the reps at that spot. >> Hey coach, based on the kind of criteria you had set for OTAs and mandatory mini camp, do you feel you all hit all of those markers? >> Yeah, and this last piece was a a first one for me candid cuz I wanted to get through the nine OTAs where we could get, you know, a few hundred snaps in in the system. So, the goal for David and Durante was to have everything they could install get put in. And even though you might not rep it a lot, the reason that's important when you do get to training camp, you've had that meeting, you've had the clips, you've had the walk-through. So, there is some recall for that. And so, goal line's not a big place that you work, you know, during a OTA, but we did install that. That's like an example of like everything's going to go in knowing that we are going to use this again at the end of July and end of August. So I like that they were detailed to put it in and then as we get into camp, we'll get there. So through those nine OTAs, that was good. And then the last piece over the last few days was really to see where we're at from an entire depth standpoint. What would that look like with more reps, more playing time? How is the communication? And so that's when different people that I, you know, kind of listed today. So okay, I want to see you a few more people this day and I think it rises the whole level of it candidly. And so that's what I was hoping to do and then build this connection together as a team. So I'm proud of the work they've done so far. By no means are we like the team that we're going to be, but I am very excited about what we can become. They've got a good edge, a good connection, a good competitive mindset. And the closer that gets, like the better we'll be. And so I'm I'm pumped about where we're at. >> Blake Lasswell. >> Coach, and playing off of that, you know, several players have talked about, you know, they've given great rave reviews as far as your coordinators. But when DeRonnie, couple of guys told me that he's one of the smartest coaches that they've already had and it's still early. You're still doing installs. So with that being said, how do you see that translating with DeRonnie to some of the younger guys like Cain or Ali or some of those guys? >> I think what he does like what his superpower is, he can like talk the play, but he can also talk like the overall like football IQ. All right, on this third down, why can't you be past the sticks in this coverage to end of that space? on a certain formation, what are the things that could hit you? So thought he's done like an exceptional job of like it's not just the plays on defense it but knowing how to apply certain things into spaces and so that's been one of the more impressive things to see them grow on the things that we're hunting on defense and what are they looking for, how can they identify them and he's put a lot of pressure on them to be able to verbalize that but that's been one example of like some exceptional teaching to do that. So, we'll do one more Nick and then you're very excited for this question so >> You you said that after watching OTAs and then mini camp last year you felt like the team didn't show like a desperation like they did in 2024. Did you see that this year and what was sort of the difference? >> Yeah. I felt and I I had to go back to like during that off season to go back to watch some of the 24 and stack it into 25 to see what was the same, what was different and um I've definitely thought this OTAs if if you'd asked a player they would agree like we've surpassed what we've been together in 2 years of like standards and speed and like the attitude to go do that together. So, um that's fair because the team in 24 got much better as it went but our early part of the OTAs and camp we were up and down quite a bit and then last year I felt just we weren't as connected and going as much that I was looking at desperation and being hungry. So, I'd say this is the new, you know, benchmark for us about what that could look like and knowing they can work their ass off and have a great time doing it. So, that would be my my take. Well, I will see you guys in a month it's important for you guys to uh take a breath too. So, we'll all uh have an intense time together for the next seven or months or so after that but uh we'll see you in a in a bit after that but I always appreciate you guys uh great questions and enjoy the dialogue. So, see you when we get back. All right. Ready to break? right. You got that right. All right. Have a good one, guys.

title: Dyami Brown talks about Jayden Daniels' command of the offense
text: How do you feel David Bile's offense get getting the hang of it over these weeks, months? How do you feel like you >> How do I feel about it? >> And how do you feel you've grown and and understanding it? >> Um feel like I've been pretty good at it. Um just getting down the details. I mean, there's a lot more to, you know, learn that I'm going to keep learning, but uh for the most part, I feel like I'm in a good spot and just keep getting better. >> How excited are you for this opportunity in this offense? You're getting a ton of work, feeling healthy. Like it it's you came in, you know, kind of midway through the year last year, but this year you get the whole off off season to spend with Jaden working on the routes, work with Terry. >> Uh confident, blessed, and just ready to, you know, play ball. U couldn't be more blessed. Um I've put in the work. I've, you know, battled through a lot of things. Never lost courage in myself. Um and just keep getting better and better each day that I'm out here. Does it feel kind of like a a new start for you having the full off season going in? >> Um I would say >> yeah honestly um this has been the >> feel like this is the first off seasonason that I've had that you know I haven't had to battle back from any injury or broken collarbone torn ACL or anything like that. So yeah, I would say so. Yeah. >> How much command is is Jaden showing at the line of scrimmage? >> Um 100%. Um he's outstanding. I mean, you couldn't ask for more from a quarterback and um you know, like we always say, we're just going to keep improving and getting better and better. >> Thanks, T. >> Sir, you're established in the league. What's it like seeing Sunny kind of go through this first off season? >> Um, you know, coming in as a rookie, you know, it's always hard adjusting, but I feel like he's doing an amazing job at doing that. Uh, he's has the green dot right now as the mic. Um, and you know, for him really, it's just being confident confident in his communication. You know, we know he can play. We know that he he was first round pick, you know, of course all that, but you know, you got to live up to that and, you know, I know he can do it. Everybody knows he can do it. It's just him at the end of the day, you know, him having that communication, him having that confidence to run the huddle and I know he can do it. >> For you, I mean, you went through the rookie routine. What are you seeing from him at this stage as a rookie? >> Man, I'm see a lot a lot of maturity um at his age. So, I think that's really huge. She's very um like involved in learning and want to get to learn. He's willing to uh make mistakes so he could grow. So, I mean, just being a rookie last year and seeing him come in this year, uh it's really impressive to see and um you know, we all making each other better. So, >> you guys still making him bring uh bring breakfast in for the room as the rookie. >> Oh, shoot. Shoot. I mean, I didn't have to That's Frank. I'll leave that up to Frankie and so >> you going to make him bring breakfast? >> Yeah, he still got to bring breakfast, you know, candy, snacks, all that. >> All right. >> You know, it's tradition. >> Yeah. Thank you. I talked to coach Pagano last week and he's so excited about the speed off the edges. What do you think you bring beyond more speed off the edge? >> Well, I mean, I'm playing inside this year, so I'm not really playing outside linebacker. >> How's that transition for you? >> It's good. I mean, it's smooth because I did that when I came into the league. This not the system, but what I'm playing I played my first two years in the league. Um, then passers wise, what I did in San Francisco is exactly what I'm doing here. Um, and then that first year can't see pass rush wise is a little bit what I'm doing here, except I'm inside to out, not outside to in. So, I I like it. Um, I think we have a really deep group. I think from the OBS to interior linemen, it's uh no drop off. I think it's a lot of very proven guys, but are still young. Like a lot of us are, it's like 25, 26, 27, 28, 29, like that area. Um, and I feel like just it's it's just a really good group. A lot of guys we know each other from being in the league, playing with each other. So, it's it's the cohesiveness is already kind of there. >> When when you get into a defensive scheme like this that's at least to us looks like it's going to show a lot of multiple fronts. There's going to be a lot of different looks. How much do you like that variety? >> I like it because I'm a versatile player. That's that's my thing. >> That's um been my thing for these last seven years. So, I like it. I like where I can be in different places. You can have different matchups. you're not always going to be in the same spot and that can give different different opportunities to different to do different things to expose weaknesses in the O line. And >> when you're when O linemen have to deal with a defense that plays multiple fronts, does that get to them at all? Just when they don't know snap after snap who they're going up against or where guys might be kind of rushing from? >> Yeah, I think it just causes more communication. And the more communication you give the offense to have, I think the the slower they'll play because I mean when they're talking too much and really not know what's going on, it cuts off their timing. So I think that's a plus about having multiple fronts in multiple different guys in multiple different spaces. >> And last one, as a guy that's been in the league for a while, what have you seen from Styles? I mean, he communicates well. Um, athletic. Um, just, you know, you got to get into games, but right, what I've seen right now, everything that you saw in college and in the combine, just really good athletic, big player that can run and um has you you can tell he has like natural leadership skills. >> Thanks very much. How's the adjustment to the pro game been for you? Do you feel like you're where you need to be? >> Um, no. I feel like I need to get better every day. That's why I prescribe myself. So, I'm never at my limit. So, I'm always reaching to be better and get >> I talked to Anthony Lynn last week and he said you're the type of player that needs pads on to really show what you can do. H how much do you want to get to the stage where there's pads on and you get to go downhill? >> Oh, man. I can't wait man. Um that's my type of party and you know, I'm just here to get better each and every day, man. Then when the pads come on, the pads come on. But pads come on. That's my type of party for sure. I like it. >> How much do you enjoy having a mini camp like this where you have an opportunity to get a couple more reps and get get a little more work in? >> Um, man, it's great, man. Just being here with the guys and just learning from these guys, man. Um, it's a dream come true, man. I'm I'm blessed to be here, man. So, I'm excited and just trying to get better each and every day. >> Has it been nice being close to home just three hours up the road? >> For sure. For sure. But I'm always trying to be here, man. I'm trying to be present, man. Home is home, but I got to be here before folks here and just trying to find ways to be better and get >> Was it cool to see Bill going through work with you guys today? >> Yeah, it was great, man. Um, Bill, he liked that, man. I'm just excited to be alongside with them boys. Everybody in the room, I feel like we all make each other better. >> Has he given you any advice? Just, you know, he went through this as a rookie last year and what you need to do to make an NFL roster and make an impact. >> Yeah, we um we always communicate with each other um stuff like that. So he always telling us little things that he see and vice versa. So everybody learning from each other. >> It's been awesome. It's been a lot of fun. I think you can tell the intent. You can tell the detail and you can tell the passion that's behind it. So had a lot of fun learning it. I think the guys have had fun. >> Dive into the the intent that you just that that kind of stuck out to me. Explain intent for us. Yeah, I just think that the coaches are very intentional with everything they're trying to bring to us and you know whether that's a route for a specific player or whether that's the detail on the specific route is is just so so there and that makes it easy as a player because you know you can trust the the purpose behind it and have a lot of fun play free. >> How about you personally? How do you feel out there and obviously you have some big goals and just much more comfortable? You look more comfortable from from our perspective. How comfortable do you feel out there? I've had a lot of fun just trying to learn every day, you know, trying to get better, trying to build comfort, build experience, and then build the build the focus that comes with learning an NFL offense. >> Yeah. >> How does Jaden look out there for you? Because obviously that's a new new new playbook for him under center a little bit more. What stood out to you about Jaden a little bit? >> It's been great. I think the way he's embraced it, the way he's learned it has been a great step of just leadership more than anything. And I think he's he's already had every skill he needed to succeed. And I just think that the way that he's embraced this for all of us is pretty special. And just the relationship that he continues to build with players, with coaches, and with everybody in this building is awesome. >> You mentioned the buzzword leadership. Um, what stood out to you about Jaden's leadership uh early on here? >> I think it's really cool to just see the operation of everything. To see Jaden in the huddle, to see Jaden in all the steps, some things that, you know, we we did a lot of great things last year and the year before, but to to have that, you know, intimate scene in a huddle and different things like that is pretty special. And so we we've enjoyed that and it's been cool to, you know, see everybody in that setting. Luke, what have you thought of? Just what Sorry, bud. >> No, you're fine. >> What do you think of Antonio so far? Lot get thrown at you as a rookie like that. >> Yeah, he's awesome. He's done really well. I think he's done everything that everybody's asked of him. He's fluid. He's a great player and uh he's he's a great addition character-wise to the room, too. So, it's it's been a lot of fun getting to know him, getting to uh play with him. >> When you watch him, does he look like a guy that could play inside and outside on this level? Yeah, I think, you know, this is one of those teams where where we value guys who can do a lot and I think he's one of those guys and it's a lot of fun to, you know, be be in a room full of those guys and it's been awesome. >> How much more do you like in the offense just more motion before pre- snap, but just more movement pre- snap? Yeah, I I think you know that helps a lot whether it's condensed, whether it's stacks, whether it's motion. You know, I think you can throw a lot at a defense and I think that you know every offense has its own corks, has its own things and hopefully that's something that we can utilize. >> What kind of differences have you noticed between uh this offseason period between last year and this year? >> I think it's really hard to put comparisons out there. You know, I think as much as you want, I know that it's easy to try to compare things, but I think that where we're at's awesome. I think we're building off where we began when we when we came out here. for what was it midappril and I think we've continued to get better every single day whether in leaps or whether in you know short shuffles and uh it's been a lot of fun to get better to compete with this group and to just kind of embrace and learn the culture. >> Like I said Jaylen is a great quarterback. He has a different dynamic to this offense and um like I said coach Blau just you know handling it the best he can and you know he's doing a great job. >> What do you think of kind of the cohesion of the receiver room as a whole? >> Uh it's great. You know we all get along. Um I think that's a good thing about our room. you know, we all, you know, push for one, push for one each other to do great out here on the field and, you know, that's what you want. And so, um, I think we got a lot of great guys in the room and, you know, we're all playing off each other. >> Well, and you've played for some dynamic offenses. Where does this one feel? I mean, granted, it's June, but you probably have a feel for what it looks like. >> Yeah, it's going to be explosive, I feel like. Um, you know, obviously, you know, like you said, it's only OTAAS and we got camp and stuff like that and throughout the summer learning and stuff like that, but you know, we're just doing building blocks right now. You know, taking it one one day at a time and, you know, u when it comes season time, you know, um, it's going to be explosive. You've played for a lot of good quarterbacks obviously and now you get to play with Jaden. What stood out to you about him in terms of the ball he throws, maybe his cadence, his command of the huddle. What stood out to you? >> Yeah, he's very accurate. You know, um he's uh and he's just commands the huddle. You know, he's focused. You can see that the drive that he has this year and how great he wants to be, you know, and coach BL's doing a great job with him just teaching the offense and he's coming out here and preparing us too as well. And so, I'm excited for him. Excited for the year that he's going to have and I know he's going to do big things. >> Oh, man. First and foremost, uh thankful to be back. Uh grateful to be back. Uh feels good to be back, you know, out here with the guys and being able just to have another opportunity to play in another season in NFL. Uh as far as new offense, uh it's been it's been coming together pretty well. Uh David Blows, he's he's a great OC. He's pretty smart, knows the game, played the game, and uh just looking forward to, you know, the season and having fun. >> The offense specifically, what do you like about it? Because obviously you're in Cliff's offense when you were here. uh what are the differences and and how does it maybe play to your strengths a little bit more? >> Uh I both I think any any any offensive coordinator is is a smart OC. You know, they they they have ways to you know manipulate the game in in different ways. I think now with with uh with Blau is it's more diversity uh a little bit more under the center. Uh still can go shotgun at the end of the day. Uh some spread offense all the things that we need to you know put players in a position to make plays and you know be a successful offense. during his press conference before practice, DQ called you out specifically for somebody that's that stood out a little bit. What do you think you brought early on here in OTAAS and mini camp? >> Uh just just energy and and the intentional details just to be able to come out here and do the things that I need to do. Uh I think right right now we want to be able to compete. Uh we're competing against each other so we want to make each other better and this is the time to do it. Uh and my goal is just to keep doing that, you know, for the rest of the time. >> Damn, what does Van Jefferson bring to this offense? Oh man, Van he's he's he's he's a a speed guy who can who can be able to stretch the field as well. Uh I think and you know we have a lot of guys that can do that. It's just you know a certain time of and when that's needed and you know I'm excited to see what Van does as well. >> I'm sure it's weird you're a veteran now too I guess technically but but what what have maybe you learned from Van so far in this uh mini camp and OTAAS? Oh man, just just stay focused. Uh stay locked in. Uh you know, because we we had a conversation like, man, we we get an opportunity to come out here and play the game that we love. It's it's another opportunity. We got a chance. They giving us a chance. So take advantage of that opportunity. >> For you and the receivers today, what was sort of the primary focus out there, >> uh just to go out there and compete. You we want to go out there and compete and be the best room. Uh I think uh a lot of the times like on on the offense side of the ball receivers can get the offense going just because we can have a little bit more plays that's more explosive for 10 plus 15 plus things like that. So we want to be out there and be the most explosive group. >> Yeah. I mean when you were here two years ago Blau was assistant quarterback's coach. Now you're here he's OC. title: NFL Commissioner Roger Goodell on the growth of Flag Football across the world | Women’s Sports Now
text: The weekend of July 24th to the 26th, the NFL Youth Flag Football Championship will take over Westfield, Indiana. Over 350 girls and boys will compete from over 12 countries in the largest flag football tournament in the world. And you can see it all across the ESPN platforms. And we get to welcome to women's sports now, the commissioner of the National Football League, Roger Goodell. Hey, I mean, I had to have my own show to get to have a show to interview you, right? >> Uh yeah. Well, yeah. It's better than the guy you live with. >> I know. I know. I hear that all the time. Um, the first thing I thought about for this season was to have you on to talk about the growth of flag football for women and for girls. So, I just love to know like how did this get on your radar in the first place? Well, uh, having twin girls who, uh, love football like crazy and never had a chance to play, um, and you can see the reaction when people do play, but I I'm most inspired by the fact that these young women, um, there's something at that point in time, particularly in those high school years, which we all know are difficult. Um, and I I know it through my daughters. Um, that self-confidence and that ability to compete and say, so many young women have said to me, I want to play a man's sport. And I just love that. Um, and I so I think we're really actually having an impact well beyond just playing flag football. It's an impact on their lives, on who they believe they are and who they can become and how they can compete. And I've just seen so many stories of that and I love it. You know, it's amazing you said that about the twins because I was curious whether they had wanted to play it. And they are slightly older than the group of girls that are growing up playing it. Over 69,000 young girls playing it this last calendar year. And one of those girls, Roger, was our daughter Taylor. And she got to play that for her middle school. Um it was actually a very um infamous football guy calling the game. I thought you might want to take a listen and take might be available for work. Um, but we do have a video that we'll play for you. Mikey, can we roll it? >> That's it. T, >> here we go, baby. >> That's it. Nice cut. Go, go, get in. Oh, no. They pulled it. They pulled it. >> No, I'm not sure how you feel about the commentary. >> Not you're That's when you're a little too close to the product, right? And I take full credit for the spin move, by the way. But you know what I love about this is that I don't have to say to her, "You can't play football. That's a boy sport." I can tell her, "Go out there and play football." What's that messaging like from the Shield to women out there? >> I think it's incredibly powerful. Um because we we want kids I want kids to play, boys and girls, men and women. I want them to play sport. I think you get so much out of playing sports. Um, and the lessons are so invaluable as you grow. I I wouldn't be anywhere without the lessons I learned from sports. It was probably the only thing I was good at as a kid. And but the reality is um for young women, I think it's even more powerful um that they able to cross over into traditionally a men's sport, but also they're incredible athletes. They're incredible people. And I just think the same things you get out of football, they can get out of flag football. And it's it's that empowerment of um and confidence that you can do a lot of things that you may not have believed before. And just crossing over to a men's sport. Uh it's no longer a men's sport. Flag is flag is for the world. And we call it a global sport. It's different from football, but it has so many of the unique nature and so many of the the values that are so valuable to um to kids as they grow up. >> I think what's really cool is like my son is six and he's playing flag football for the first time this year. He's been playing lots of sports and girls are always on the sports teams with him. So, I think that sets a great precedent that he knows that he has to play alongside girls as well and they're just as good as him. but this fall he's playing flag football for the first time and he is playing against a team that is being coached by Aaron Donald and I was wondering if you could give me any advice on how to navigate that. >> Maybe you should get Aaron to come back into the NFL. >> Yeah, I know. How do I get Miles Garrett to adopt my son so that he can coach my son Steve? >> You know, I you know I had the same thing. Um and this was another inspiring moment a couple years ago. Steve Young, I was at 49er game and Steve Young came up to say hi. And he said, "I'm here with our two daughters. They're playing flag football and I'm here with the whole team. Would you come say hi to them?" I said, "Instead of that, just come on up. I'd love to have them all come up." So, they all came up and I had a blast with them. But Steve, when Steve spoke about coaching football and particularly his daughters and young women, he said, "I fell in love with the game again." and and I maybe it just opened up why I fell in love with the game in the first place. And so I love when NFL players are going back and coaching their kids. Um I I just think it has the greatest statement of how important it is to them, uh how much they support them and how you're in the right place when you're out on that field. >> And it's just so important for the men in their lives to play these roles. I mean, look at the Stafford family with all those beautiful girls out there, >> you know, and those girls will probably end up doing the same thing. I know for Rich like he loves being a part of teaching the game to women and Sarah and I were talking about it that the female fans of the Shield are one of the fastest growing demos that there is. So how does there how do you apply this love of the game for women to the greater Shield itself? And how does that translate to flag football? >> Well, you know, data shows that if you play the game, you are more likely to be a lifelong fan. And I I don't I think that's um I think that's a true statement and and a fact. Um so if young women are playing the game and they're getting that exposure early on, both of our daughters, uh yours and and mine, um they had the opportunity to be exposed to football and that's why they fell in love with it. And I've always said, you know, it used to be that, you know, the guys used to say, "Hey, I'm going down in the basement. I'm watching football. I'll see you at dinner." Or they go off for Sunday afternoon play. and go to a football game. Now they're going with the family. And when I when I go to a game, the one number one thing I look at is in the stands. I'm looking to see how many women are there, how many families are there, how many young people are there. That audience mix has changed dramatically, uh, in our stadiums. Uh, it changes at our events. The draft, um, I can't even tell you, it's it's probably 50/50 at the draft. And I I just think that's a a really uh significant thing for the growth of the NFL to have a fan base. Listen, women are fans, too. And they're awful good fans. They're great fans. And as you know, um they usually make the decisions around the house. And so that's a good thing, right? >> Yeah. And they usually spend the money on >> That's what I always say. I was like, I hold the purse string. So if you if you want a jersey, you better ask me first. Um, I do want to talk about the Olympics a little bit because I'm very excited about flag football becoming an Olympic sport. I've been waiting for it for a long time. And you know, to become an Olympic sport, you have to be played in a certain amount of countries around the world. So, how are you guys able to grow the game internationally in order to make it an Olympic sport? Um I think by just offering it ultimately you know you have to work the Olympic structure is is slightly different but if you want to be a global sport and that's what we want to do you have to be an Olympic sport um because it's the greatest in my view international platform for sports um and they have rules about different number of countries as you point out the number of players we have exceeded all that and you have to work through the federation system so every there's There's a a federation president in charge of football on a global basis and then there federations of each country. And frankly, it was just making the game available to them, showing them how to organize, showing them how easy it is to play. And one of the key things about flag football is making it accessible. Um, it's not expensive. Uh, you don't need a a lot of equipment. Uh, you can run out on most any field uh, and play. Um, and that you see these these young women right here, a lot of those were our ambassadors and they are the most amazing young women I've ever met. Um, they're just extraordinary and um, we're really proud of them and I think that you're going to see that they will inspire thousands and thousands and thousands of people to play the game. What will it be, sorry, what will it be like for you as a girl dad to watch the women carrying the flag in marching in the opening ceremonies for the Olympics? >> Now you get me. >> Um, uh, I think it's going to be a moment that, um, people will really recognize that it does have an impact on young women and they get they can play this game and they're going to play it at the highest level at that point in time. Now, as you guys know, we're starting a pro flag league for women and men, but there obviously there this is going to be a really important moment for us and we've tried to build that infrastructure of, you know, having it available as young kids to be able to play, then getting into high school, then getting into college, then getting into the Olympics, then getting into the NFL, and all of that infrastructure. Young women are are starting to get scholarships into colleges now to play flag football. That's great for a lot of young women that that could be financially available or they can get to a different school that they might want to get into. All that's great for us and I think the Olympics is going to be that moment where they're going to see that on a global basis in every country. And I got to tell you, it's no shoe that the US is going to win. Um Mexico has a great team. China's working hard to beat uh and has done incredibly well in the Asian-Pacific series, their European teams. It's going to be competitive and everyone's going to want to beat us on our own property in the in LA in 28, but I think it's going to be the start of a movement um or at least another big stairst step in our movement. >> Do you envision NFL players either current or legends playing in the Olympics in flag football? >> Absolutely. um we approved it a year ago. Um and I've had a lot of players um that have said we want to we want to participate in that. It sets up really well because it's before camps. Uh it'll be the first week of the Olympics next year. Um listen, there's these these players are competitors. Um and they love the big stage and to win a gold medal or any medal is something I think they would all treasure and they talk about it all the time. So, I I absolutely believe we're gonna have players in the Olympics, active players, and probably some retired players if they can stay up with them. So, >> uh I I just have one more uh really quick question. Um one of my favorite things that's happened in the NFL lately is female referees. Um I would just like to make a plea that only referees can be female because who better at telling men what they are doing wrong? Um, I feel like we are overqualified for this job and while I just had you, I just want to just put it out there that I think it's one of the greatest things you guys have done. Just from a woman's perspective, watching our inclusion in the game, that was a really big first step for me and it meant a lot. >> I thought you were going to ask him to overturn the Falcons Patriots. >> I thought about doing that um as a Falcons fan. Um, but I don't think he has the power to do that unless you have a time machine. >> You are right, sir. I don't even if I didn't have a time machine uh area, if I did have one, I couldn't do that. But if you had um if you had met Sarah Thomas, who was the first female official we had on the field, um she's an extraordinary woman and um she has opened a lot of doors and I think it's just great that she's been a part of the NFL. She's made the NFL better. >> A great >> Roger, thank you so much for taking the time to be with us. It means a lot to us. >> I'm always glad to see you. Um good luck with the show. We're always here rooting for you.
